Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the market-entry authorisation gate for Licensing & Appointments — no solicitation in a country or state until the authorisation matrix shows an effective grant for that class; escalates disputed scope to Regulatory Counsel

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — IDD (EU) 2016/97 Art. 18 (identity, register and verification disclosure) and Arts. 4 and 6 (freedom of establishment / freedom of services passport notification) re-read on EUR-Lex at each market-entry case; US leg re-read against the target state's insurance code authorisation article and the NAIC UCAA Expansion instructions in force on the application date

In-scope processes.value: Market entry and class expansion: new country/state entry, new Solvency II Annex I class or NAIC line of authority, new legal entity or branch, and any renewal of business in a jurisdiction where the grant was previously restricted or suspended

In-scope systems.value: The authorisation matrix (entity × jurisdiction × class × effective date) held in the Internal Regulatory System and pushed as a hard bind gate into the Underwriting Platform and Broker & Agent Portal

Compliance procedure documented.value: Market-Entry Authorisation Procedure — class mapping (Annex I / NAIC LOA), gap analysis against the existing grant, Art. 6 FOS or Art. 4 FOE notification to the home NCA, UCAA Expansion for US states, register-verification capture, and the Art. 18 disclosure wording refresh

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and countersigned by Regulatory Counsel; re-approved on any EIOPA passporting decision change, host-state general good notice, or UCAA instruction revision

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per market entry — the home NCA has one month from a complete Art. 6 notification to transmit to the host NCA, and distribution may not start until the home NCA confirms transmission; US state CoA grants are tracked to their issue date and to the annual entity renewal/registration date

Deadline reminders configured.value: Authorisation case milestones alert at notification+30 days (transmission chase), grant date minus 30 days (system gate configuration) and annually at CoA renewal minus 60 days

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Certificates of Authority, UCAA acknowledgements, home-NCA notification acknowledgements and host-NCA transmission confirmations, dated EIOPA/state register lookups, and the class-mapping worksheet retained 10 years from surrender of the authorisation

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any quote, bind or renewal in a jurisdiction or class not on the authorisation matrix at the transaction date is logged as an unauthorised-business exception with root cause, book size exposed and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Counsel signs off every class-scope interpretation, every restricted or conditioned grant, and every unauthorised-business remediation including any self-report to the host NCA or state DOI

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All policies bound and renewed in the period, keyed by writing entity, jurisdiction and class code, joined to the authorisation matrix as it stood on each bind date — plus every market-entry case opened in the period

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — a single bind in an unauthorised jurisdiction/class, or a distribution start before home-NCA transmission was confirmed, fails the test and goes to the Head of Compliance the same day

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per market entry; testing is semi-annual over the bind population plus 100% re-performance of every market-entry case opened since the last test

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not sit in Licensing & Appointments and must not have prepared or approved any sampled authorisation case

Evidence location for test results.value: Semi-annual authorisation-coverage workpaper (bind extract, matrix as-at snapshot, register lookups, exception schedule) in the compliance evidence repository under Licensing & Appointments

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Authorisation matrix export with effective dates, CoA and passport notification pack per jurisdiction, and the Art. 18 disclosure specimen in use — producible for a host NCA general-good enquiry or a state market conduct exam within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Affairs Manager fronts host NCA and state DOI enquiries through the home NCA relationship; Regulatory Counsel clears any written admission of business written outside the grant before it leaves the building

checklist.step: Open the market-entry authorisation case
actions: Take the signed market-entry request from the Head of Distribution and record in the Internal Regulatory System: writing legal entity, NAIC co-code or LEI, target country/state, intended start date, distribution model (own employees, tied agents, brokers) and expected first-year premium.
Set the case type to 'Freedom of Services', 'Freedom of Establishment / branch' or 'US state Certificate of Authority' — the route decides every downstream step.
Attach the board or executive committee approval for the entry and the draft business plan for the jurisdiction.
Assign the case a target authorisation-effective date and back-schedule from it.
checklist.done: the case record names entity, jurisdiction, route, distribution model and target effective date with the entry approval attached.

checklist.step: Fix the exact classes of business to be written
actions: Sit with the Insurance Product Manager and list every product intended for the jurisdiction, including add-ons and assistance covers sold alongside.

Map each product to Solvency II Annex I class numbers (e.g. class 8 fire and natural forces, class 13 general liability, class 16 miscellaneous financial loss) for EU entries, and to the state's NAIC lines of authority for US entries.
Flag any product that is an insurance-based investment product (IBIP) — it drags in Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/2359 obligations and usually a separate permission.
Write the class list onto the case as the authoritative scope; anything not on it may not be quoted.
checklist.done: every intended product is mapped to a named Annex I class or NAIC line of authority on the case scope list.

checklist.step: Pull the current authorisation inventory for the entity
actions: Export the entity's current authorisation matrix rows: each jurisdiction, each class, grant date, any restriction, and the source document reference.
Retrieve the underlying certificates — the home NCA authorisation decision for EU entities, and the Certificate of Authority PDF for each US state.
Check each certificate for conditions on its face (class limits, premium caps, deposit conditions, prohibition on writing new business).
Note any grant whose renewal or annual registration is overdue and hand it to the renewal tracker before it blocks the expansion.
checklist.done: the current grant per jurisdiction and class is listed with its source certificate and any face conditions.

checklist.step: Produce the gap list between requested scope and existing grant
actions: Build a grid of requested class × jurisdiction and mark each cell COVERED, NOT COVERED or COVERED WITH CONDITION.
For COVERED cells paste the certificate reference and grant date that proves it.
For NOT COVERED cells decide the instrument needed: new Art. 6 FOS notification, Art. 4 branch notification, UCAA Expansion application, or a class amendment to the existing home-state licence.
Send the gap grid to the Head of Distribution so the launch plan only contains covered or in-flight cells.
checklist.done: every requested class/jurisdiction cell is marked with its coverage status and, where uncovered, the instrument that will close it.

checklist.step: Lodge the Art. 6 freedom-of-services notification with the home NCA
actions: Draft the notification to the home supervisor naming the host Member State, the classes to be pursued and the nature of the risks or commitments to be covered, per IDD Art. 6(1).
Submit it through the home NCA's regulated-firm portal (for example the Central Bank of Ireland ONR return or BaFin's MVP portal) and record the submission reference and date on the case.
Diarise the one-month statutory window in which the home NCA must communicate the notification to the host NCA.
Do not release any marketing into the host state until the home NCA confirms transmission and the host communication period has run — record that confirmation on the case.
checklist.done: the FOS notification is lodged, its reference recorded, and the home NCA's transmission confirmation is on file before any host-state activity.

checklist.step: Lodge the Art. 4 establishment notification where a branch or permanent presence is used
actions: Where distribution runs through a branch, agency or any permanent presence, prepare the Art. 4 notification: host Member State, branch address, the person responsible for the branch's management, and the classes to be distributed.

Confirm with the Head of Distribution whether the local arrangement is genuinely a permanent presence — a tied agent operating exclusively for the entity in the host state usually is, and misclassifying it as FOS is the classic failure here.
Submit through the home NCA portal, record the reference, and diarise the one-month transmission window plus the host NCA's period to state applicable general-good rules.
Log the host NCA's general-good conditions when received and route them to Market Conduct Compliance for procedure updates.
checklist.done: the establishment notification is lodged for every permanent presence, and any host general-good conditions received are logged and routed.

checklist.step: Build and file the US Certificate of Authority expansion application
actions: Open the current UCAA Expansion Application instructions on the NAIC UCAA page and pull the state-specific checklist for the target state.

Assemble the primary application items: Uniform Application form, biographical affidavits with third-party verification for officers and directors, plan of operation with three-year pro-forma, most recent audited statutory statements, certificate of compliance from the domiciliary state, and the state's filing fee.
Confirm the lines requested on the application exactly match the case scope list — a line omitted here cannot be written later without reapplying.
Submit to the state Department of Insurance by its stated channel, record the state file number, and log every deficiency letter with its response due date.
checklist.done: the expansion application is filed with the requested lines matching the case scope, and the state file number is on the case.

checklist.step: Prove capital, deposit and registered-agent prerequisites are met
actions: Read the target jurisdiction's minimum paid-in capital and surplus requirement for each requested line and compare it to the entity's current capital and surplus per the latest statutory statement.
Where a statutory deposit is required, arrange it with Treasury and obtain the custodian's deposit certificate naming the state as beneficiary.
Appoint or confirm the registered agent / agent for service of process for the state and file the appointment form.
Record each prerequisite, its evidence document and its date on the case — a grant issued on an unmet prerequisite fails at first examination.
checklist.done: capital, deposit and service-of-process prerequisites each have a dated evidence document attached to the case.

checklist.step: Verify the entity's public register entry and capture it
actions: For EU entries, open the EIOPA insurance-undertakings and insurance-intermediaries registers and the home NCA's own register, search the entity, and confirm the entry shows the entity name, registration number and the passported host states.
For US entries, look the entity up in the state Department of Insurance company search and in the NAIC company lookup, and confirm the lines of authority shown match the grant.
Print each register page to PDF named <jurisdiction>-register-<yyyy-mm-dd>.pdf and file it on the case.
Where the register does not yet show the entry, chase the NCA or DOI in writing and hold the launch — the customer must be able to verify the entry under Art. 18.
checklist.done: a dated register capture exists for every jurisdiction and shows the entity with the intended classes.

checklist.step: Refresh the Art. 18 pre-contract disclosure to match the grant
actions: Update the pre-contract disclosure text for the jurisdiction so it states the distributor's identity and address, that it is an insurance undertaking (not an intermediary), the register in which it is entered, and the means for the customer to verify that entry.
Add the out-of-court complaint and redress bodies available in that host state (for example the national ombudsman or FIN-NET member) with contact details.
Send the drafted text to Regulatory Counsel for legal clearance and to the local language service for translation into the host state's official language.
Hand the cleared text to the Digital Channel Manager and Policy Forms Specialist for loading into quote journeys and issue packs before the launch date.
checklist.done: cleared, translated Art. 18 disclosure text naming the register, verification route and host-state redress bodies is loaded into the quote and issue packs.

checklist.step: Load the grant into the authorisation matrix with effective dates
actions: On receipt of the Certificate of Authority or the home NCA transmission confirmation, create one matrix row per entity × jurisdiction × class.
Enter the authorisation effective date, any expiry or annual-renewal date, and the certificate document link.
Enter any restriction verbatim in the condition field (for example 'personal lines only', 'no new business pending plan approval').
Mark the case status 'Authorised — effective <date>' and notify the Head of Distribution and the UW Operations Manager.
checklist.done: the matrix carries one dated, document-linked row per entity, jurisdiction and class, with conditions recorded verbatim.

checklist.step: Arm the bind gate in the underwriting and portal systems
actions: Configure the Underwriting Platform rule set so a quote whose risk jurisdiction and class code has no effective matrix row on the requested inception date is blocked, not warned.
Mirror the same block in the Broker & Agent Portal so external distributors cannot submit into an unauthorised jurisdiction or class.
Test the gate with a deliberate out-of-scope quote in the pre-production environment and screenshot the block message.
Give the Underwriting Director / Manager the list of blocked class/jurisdiction combinations so referrals are not worked around manually.
checklist.done: an out-of-scope test quote is hard-blocked in both the underwriting platform and the broker portal, with the block evidenced by screenshot.

checklist.step: Hold distribution until the authorisation is genuinely effective
actions: Keep the jurisdiction off the producer appointment plan, the marketing calendar and the broker onboarding list until Licensing & Appointments confirms the effective date.
Withdraw any pre-launch collateral, landing page or broker pack that names the jurisdiction if the grant slips.
Brief territory and broker relationship managers in writing that solicitation, quoting and even indicative pricing in the jurisdiction is prohibited before the effective date.
Record the go-live authorisation from the Producer Compliance Manager in the launch record before the first campaign goes out.
checklist.done: no solicitation, collateral or indicative pricing is live in the jurisdiction before the recorded authorisation effective date.

checklist.step: Work the conditions and deficiencies attached to a grant
actions: Raise a tracker item for each condition on the certificate or each host-state general-good rule notified, with the owning function and the date it must be satisfied by.
For deficiency letters from a state DOI, record the response due date on receipt and assign the drafter — most states allow a short fixed window before the application is closed.
Where a condition restricts classes or volumes, reflect it in the matrix condition field and in the bind gate rules the same week.
Close a tracker item only on documented evidence, not on assurance.
checklist.done: every certificate condition, general-good rule and deficiency letter has a tracked owner, due date and documented closure.

checklist.step: File the authorisation evidence pack for retention
actions: Assemble the pack: class-mapping worksheet, gap grid, notification submissions and acknowledgements, transmission confirmations, certificates of authority, register captures, Art. 18 disclosure specimen and the bind-gate test screenshot.
File it in the compliance evidence repository under Licensing & Appointments / <entity> / <jurisdiction> / <effective year>.
Apply the 10-years-from-surrender retention label so the record survives a withdrawal from the market.
Confirm the pack is indexed and retrievable by entity, jurisdiction, class and effective date.
checklist.done: the authorisation pack is filed, retention-labelled and retrievable by entity, jurisdiction and class.

testing.step: Build the population of bound and renewed business by jurisdiction and class
actions: Extract every policy bound, renewed or endorsed onto a new class in the period, with writing entity, risk jurisdiction, class/line code, inception date and written premium.
Add facultative and delegated-authority business written by coverholders and MGAs so binder business cannot hide outside the extract.
Reconcile total written premium in the extract to the period's statutory premium by state/country and clear any difference before sampling.
testing.done: the extract reconciles to reported written premium by jurisdiction and is signed as complete by the extractor.

testing.step: Reconcile every bind to an authorisation row effective on the bind date
actions: Take the point-in-time snapshot of the authorisation matrix and join each population row on entity + jurisdiction + class.
Test that the matrix row's effective date is on or before the bind date and that no expiry or suspension had bitten.
List every unmatched bind, every bind before the effective date, and every bind under a condition that excluded it, as automatic exceptions with the premium exposed.
testing.done: every bind is matched to an authorisation effective on its bind date or listed as an exception with premium quantified.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of market-entry cases opened or made effective in the period.
Take 25 bound policies selected at random with a recorded seed from the highest-premium five jurisdictions, plus every jurisdiction entered in the last 24 months.
Record population size, seed, selection date and stratification in the workpaper so the sample is reproducible.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all recent market entries, and its method is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the class mapping on the sampled cases
actions: For each sampled case, read the product wording and independently map it to Solvency II Annex I classes or the state's lines of authority without reading the case scope list first.
Compare your mapping to the recorded scope; a product written under an adjacent class is an exception even where a grant exists for that adjacent class.
Check specifically that IBIPs were identified and not mapped as ordinary life, and that assistance and legal-expenses add-ons carry their own class.
Note the source article or statute relied on for each mapping in the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled case has an independent class mapping with its source, and every divergence is logged.

testing.step: Trace passport notifications to home-NCA acknowledgement and transmission
actions: For each sampled EU entry, open the home NCA portal submission record and read the submission date and reference.
Confirm a transmission confirmation to the host NCA exists and recompute whether it fell inside the one-month window in IDD Art. 6.
Compare the date distribution actually started in the host state — first quote, first marketing send, first bind — to the transmission confirmation date.
Any activity before transmission confirmation is a reportable breach, not a documentation exception.
testing.done: every sampled EU entry shows a lodged notification, a transmission confirmation, and no host activity before it.

testing.step: Verify each sampled US grant in the source of record
actions: For each sampled US state, open the state Department of Insurance company search and the NAIC company lookup and pull the entity's licence status and lines of authority.
Compare the lines shown by the regulator to the lines on the authorisation matrix and to the lines actually written in the population.
Read the certificate of authority PDF held on the case and confirm the issue date, licence number and any face conditions match the matrix row.
Screenshot the regulator lookup into the workpaper with its retrieval date.
testing.done: regulator-held licence status and lines agree with the matrix for every sampled US state, or the difference is logged.

testing.step: Verify the public register entry supports the Art. 18 disclosure
actions: Take the live Art. 18 disclosure text used in each sampled jurisdiction from the current quote journey and issue pack.
Follow the verification route the text gives the customer — open the named register, run the search exactly as instructed, and confirm the entity is found.
Confirm the text names the entity's address, states that it is an undertaking rather than an intermediary, and lists the host-state out-of-court redress body.
A disclosure that names a register the customer cannot actually search from the given instructions is a fail.
testing.done: the disclosure's stated register and verification route resolve to a live entry for every sampled jurisdiction.

testing.step: Re-perform the bind gate control
actions: Attempt a test quote in the non-production environment for an entity/jurisdiction/class combination with no matrix row and record the system response.
Repeat through the Broker & Agent Portal under an external broker login.
Attempt a second test with an inception date one day before the matrix effective date to prove the date logic, not just the presence logic.
Capture both responses; a warning message that can be overridden counts as a control failure.
testing.done: both channels hard-block out-of-scope and pre-effective-date attempts, evidenced by captured responses.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, exposure and owner
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception carrying policy count, written premium exposed, jurisdiction, class and the date range affected.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list: class mis-mapping, matrix not updated on grant, gate rule not deployed, activity before transmission confirmation, condition ignored.
Assign an owner and a remediation date, and open a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel for any unauthorised-business finding.
Carry every open issue into the next semi-annual test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with quantified exposure, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report
actions: Compute the exception count and exposed premium against the zero-tolerance threshold.
State the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper references behind each element.
Have the independent reviewer, who prepared none of the sampled cases, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any unauthorised-business exposure to the Risk & Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, quantified exposure and a committee reporting date is filed in the repository.

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any solicitation, application submission or commission payment by a producer without an active licence and matching line of authority on that date is logged with the business written, states affected and remediation

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every appointment made on an exception, every unlicensed-solicitation remediation and every commission clawback or escheat decision arising from it

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All producers who submitted an application, bound business or received commission in the period, joined to their PDB licence history, plus all new producer onboardings completed in the period

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly producer-licensing test workpaper (population extract, PDB re-pulls, sample schedule, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository under Distribution Compliance

checklist.step: Capture the producer's identity and licence identifiers at onboarding
actions: Open the onboarding case handed over by the Agency Relations Manager and record legal name, date of birth, business address, and the National Producer Number (NPN).
Where the producer is an agency, record the firm NPN and the FEIN, and list the individual producers who will solicit under it.
For EU intermediaries record the national register number and the home Member State register that holds it.
Reject the case back to Distribution where the NPN or register number is missing — no verification can start without an identifier.
checklist.done: the case carries a verified NPN or national register number for the producer and, for agencies, the firm identifier plus the sub-producer list.

checklist.step: Pull the NIPR Producer Database report
actions: In NIPR Gateway open the PDB report request and search by NPN (never by name alone — name searches return look-alike producers).
Order the full PDB report including licence, line-of-authority, appointment and regulatory-action sections.
Save the returned report as PDF named <NPN>-PDB-<yyyy-mm-dd>.pdf onto the onboarding case.
Where the NPN returns no record, obtain the resident state licence number from the producer and resolve the identity before proceeding.
checklist.done: a dated full PDB report is attached to the case and matches the producer's identity.

checklist.step: Confirm the resident licence is active and in good standing
actions: Read the PDB licence section and confirm the resident state licence status is Active — not Expired, Inactive, Suspended, Revoked or Pending.
Check the licence expiry date is beyond the intended appointment date; a licence expiring inside 30 days goes to the renewal tracker before appointment.
Confirm the licence class (producer, agency, adjuster, surplus lines broker) is the class the role actually requires.
Record status, licence number, issue and expiry dates on the verification record.
checklist.done: the resident licence is recorded as Active with class and expiry captured, or the case is held.

checklist.step: Match lines of authority to the products the producer will sell
actions: Take the intended product list for the producer from the Head of Distribution — personal lines, commercial lines, life, variable products, IBIPs.
Compare each product to the lines of authority on the PDB report state by state: Property, Casualty, Life, Accident & Health, Variable Life & Variable Annuity.
Where the producer will sell variable annuities or unit-linked IBIPs, confirm the variable line of authority and, where applicable, the securities registration held alongside it.
Write the approved product-to-line mapping onto the case and restrict the producer's product catalogue in the portal to that mapping.
checklist.done: each intended product maps to a line of authority the producer actually holds in each state, and the portal catalogue is restricted accordingly.

checklist.step: Verify non-resident licences for every state the producer will write in
actions: List the states in the producer's intended territory from the appointment plan.
For each state read the PDB non-resident licence row and confirm status, lines of authority and expiry.
Where a state is missing, run the NIPR Gateway non-resident licence application for that state and record the transaction number and expected turnaround.
Block the state in the portal territory settings until the non-resident licence shows Active in a fresh PDB pull.
checklist.done: every intended state shows an active non-resident licence with the required lines, or is blocked in the producer's territory.

checklist.step: Review the regulatory-action and administrative-history section
actions: Read the PDB Regulatory Actions section and list every action with its state, date, reason code and disposition.
Pull the underlying order from the acting state's DOI enforcement page for any action involving fraud, misappropriation of premium, misrepresentation or licence revocation.
Where any felony or breach-of-trust matter appears, route the case straight into the 18 U.S.C. §1033 consent screening before any appointment decision.

Record a written good-repute assessment on the case, referencing IDD Art. 10(3) for EU intermediaries — a clean criminal record for property-crime and financial-crime offences and no undischarged bankruptcy.
checklist.done: every regulatory action is listed with its order reviewed, and a written good-repute assessment is on the case.

checklist.step: Verify EU intermediaries in the home Member State register
actions: Open the home Member State register named by the intermediary (for example the FCA Financial Services Register, BaFin Vermittlerregister, or ORIAS in France) and search the register number.
Confirm the entry shows the intermediary as registered, the categories of distribution permitted, and any passporting into the states where they will sell.
Confirm the entry is current in the EIOPA insurance-intermediaries register, which consolidates national registers.
Print the register page to PDF with its retrieval date and file it — this is also the evidence supporting the Art. 18 disclosure the intermediary must give customers.
checklist.done: a dated home-register and EIOPA register capture confirms the intermediary's registration and permitted categories.

checklist.step: Confirm knowledge, ability and continuing-training prerequisites
actions: For EU intermediaries confirm the Art. 10(2) minimum professional knowledge evidence — Annex I areas covering the products distributed, insurance ethics and conflicts handling — is on file.
Enrol the producer in the company's pre-solicitation training path in the LMS: product training for their approved catalogue, demands-and-needs and suitability, complaints handling and anti-fraud.
Set the 15-hours-per-year continuing professional training target for EU intermediaries and the state CE requirement for US producers on their LMS profile.
Hold the appointment where any mandatory pre-solicitation module is incomplete.
checklist.done: professional knowledge evidence is on file and every pre-solicitation module is completed in the LMS with a dated transcript.

checklist.step: Take the appointment-eligibility decision and record it
actions: Review the verification record: PDB status, line match, non-resident coverage, regulatory actions, register capture and training completion.
Set the decision to Eligible, Eligible with restriction (named states, named lines, supervision requirement) or Not eligible, and write the reason.
Where the decision is Eligible with restriction, enter the restriction in the producer record so the portal and commission systems enforce it.
Stamp the record with reviewer name, decision date and the PDB report reference relied on.
checklist.done: a stamped eligibility decision with a written reason and any restriction is on the producer record.

checklist.step: Re-pull the PDB immediately before submitting the appointment
actions: Where the eligibility decision is older than 30 days, order a fresh PDB report before the appointment transaction — status can change between decision and appointment.
Compare the fresh report to the report relied on: any change in licence status, expiry, lines or regulatory actions reopens the decision.
Attach the fresh report to the case as the appointment-date evidence.
Only then release the case to Licensing Ops for the state appointment transaction.
checklist.done: a PDB pull dated within 30 days of the appointment submission is on file and shows no adverse change.

checklist.step: Block solicitation until eligibility is live in the downstream systems
actions: Confirm the Broker & Agent Portal grants the producer access only to the approved product catalogue and approved states from the eligibility record.
Confirm the commission platform will not pay on business written outside those states and lines.
Instruct the Agency Relations Manager in writing that quoting, illustrating and even pre-qualifying a customer counts as solicitation and is prohibited until access goes live.
Record the access go-live date on the producer record as the earliest permitted solicitation date.
checklist.done: portal access, product catalogue and commission eligibility all reflect the decision, and the earliest permitted solicitation date is recorded.

checklist.step: Subscribe the producer to continuous licence-status monitoring
actions: Add the NPN to the NIPR Alerts / PDB subscription so status changes, expirations, cancellations and new regulatory actions are pushed daily.
Route the alert feed into the agency/producer management system so a status change automatically flips the eligibility flag to Suspended pending review.
Set the daily exception queue owner and a 1-business-day service level for working alerts.
Test the feed with a known status change and confirm the flag flipped.
checklist.done: the producer is on the alert subscription and a test status change is shown to suspend eligibility automatically.

checklist.step: Re-verify on any change of state, line, agency or entity
actions: Treat any request to add a state, add a line of authority, move to a different agency, or change from individual to firm writing as a new verification, not an amendment.
Re-pull the PDB, re-run the line match against the expanded product list, and re-take the eligibility decision.
Where the producer moves agency, confirm the prior agency's appointment is terminated before the new appointment is submitted so appointment records do not double-count.
Record the trigger event on the verification record so the reason for each re-verification is auditable.
checklist.done: each change trigger has its own dated verification record with a fresh PDB pull and a restated decision.

checklist.step: Handle failed or lapsed verifications and any business already written
actions: Where a producer is found to have solicited or submitted before an active licence existed, pull the affected applications and policies from the policy administration system by producer code and date range.
Quantify policies, premium and commission paid, and freeze further commission on the affected book.
Raise a tracker issue with root cause, the states affected and the remediation plan, and take the Regulatory Counsel decision on state notification.
Where commission was paid to an unlicensed producer, execute the clawback or the state-specific handling and document it.
checklist.done: affected business is quantified, commission is frozen or clawed back, and a counsel decision on notification is recorded.

checklist.step: File the verification evidence pack
actions: Assemble the pack per producer: dated PDB reports, register captures, line-match worksheet, good-repute assessment, LMS transcript and the stamped eligibility decision.
File under Distribution Compliance / Producer Licensing / <NPN> in the compliance evidence repository.
Apply the 7-years-after-termination retention label.
Confirm the pack is retrievable by NPN, producer name, state and appointment date.
checklist.done: each producer's verification pack is filed, retention-labelled and retrievable by NPN and state.

testing.step: Build the population of producing and newly onboarded producers
actions: Extract every producer who submitted an application, bound a policy or received a commission payment in the period, with NPN, states written, lines written and first production date.
Add every onboarding case completed in the period regardless of whether production followed.
Reconcile the producer count and commission total to the commission platform ledger for the period and clear differences before sampling.
testing.done: the population reconciles to paid commission and production records and is signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile every producing producer to a verification record
actions: Join the population to verification records on NPN and confirm a stamped eligibility decision exists dated before the first production date.
Flag producers with no verification record, with a decision dated after first production, or whose PDB evidence pre-dates the appointment by more than 30 days.
Flag producers producing in a state or line not on their eligibility record.
Treat each flag as an automatic exception without judgement.
testing.done: every producing producer is matched to a pre-dated verification or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of producers with any regulatory action on the PDB and 100% of intermediaries onboarded from EU registers.
Take 40 producers at random with a recorded seed, stratified across the largest three distribution channels and across new versus established relationships.
Record population size, strata, seed and draw date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all regulatory-action and EU-register producers, and its method is documented.

testing.step: Re-pull the PDB independently for each sampled producer
actions: Order a fresh PDB report by NPN from NIPR Gateway on the test date, independent of anything held on the case.
Compare licence status, class, expiry, lines of authority by state, and regulatory actions to what the verification record asserted.
Where the report shows an expiry or cancellation that pre-dates production, extend testing to all business written after that date.
File the fresh reports in the workpaper with their retrieval dates.
testing.done: an independently pulled PDB report supports or contradicts each sampled verification, and contradictions are extended.

testing.step: Re-perform the line-of-authority match against business actually written
actions: For each sampled producer, extract the policies they wrote in the period with state, product and line code.
Compare each written line to the lines the fresh PDB shows the producer held in that state on the bind date.
Pay particular attention to variable annuity and unit-linked IBIP sales written on a Life-only authority.
Any policy written outside the held authority is a reportable breach with the premium quantified, not a documentation exception.
testing.done: every sampled policy is written under a line of authority held in that state on the bind date, or the breach is quantified.

testing.step: Verify EU register entries independently
actions: For each sampled EU intermediary, search the home Member State register and the EIOPA intermediaries register on the test date.
Confirm the registration is live, the permitted distribution categories cover the products sold, and any passporting covers the states of sale.
Compare to the capture held on the case and note any lapse between them.
Screenshot each register result with its retrieval date into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled EU intermediary's live registration and permitted categories are confirmed and captured.

testing.step: Test the good-repute and training prerequisites
actions: For each sampled producer with a regulatory action, read the written good-repute assessment and the underlying state order and judge whether the conclusion survives the facts.
Pull the LMS transcript and confirm every pre-solicitation module was completed before the first production date, with dates.
For EU intermediaries confirm the Art. 10(2) knowledge evidence covers the product categories actually sold and that the 15-hour annual training target is on the profile.
Log training completed after first production as an exception with the number of days exposed.
testing.done: every sampled producer's good-repute assessment and pre-solicitation training completion are verified against dated evidence.

testing.step: Re-perform the continuous monitoring control
actions: Take the NIPR alert feed for the period and list every status change, expiry and new regulatory action received.
For each, check the eligibility flag in the producer management system changed within the 1-business-day service level.
Check whether any business was written by that producer between the alert date and the flag change and quantify it.
Sample 10 alerts and trace end to end from the feed entry to the portal access change.
testing.done: each sampled alert is shown to have suspended eligibility within the service level, with any intervening business quantified.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, exposure and owner
actions: Raise one issue per exception with NPN, states, lines, policy count, premium and commission exposed.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list: no verification performed, name-based rather than NPN-based search, stale PDB at appointment, line mismatch, alert not worked, register lapse.
Assign an owner and remediation date, and refer unlicensed-solicitation findings to Regulatory Counsel for the state notification decision.
Carry open issues forward as mandatory retest rows in the next quarterly test.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with quantified exposure, root cause, owner, remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the verification-defect rate against the 2% threshold and count unlicensed-solicitation breaches against the zero threshold.
State the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with workpaper references for each assertion tested.
Have the independent reviewer, who performed none of the sampled verifications, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Distribution Compliance forum and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with defect rate, breach count, stated conclusion and reporting date is filed in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Licensing Ops owner for appointment and termination transactions — submits every NIPR appointment inside the state's post-first-application window and every termination inside the state's notice window; escalates cause determinations to the Producer Compliance Manager

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — IDD (EU) 2016/97 Art. 17(1) (honest, fair and professional conduct in the customer's best interests) and Art. 30(3) with Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/2359 Art. 16 read at each procedure review; the statutory appointment and termination windows re-read state by state in the NIPR appointment/termination business rules and the state's producer licensing statute before each cycle

In-scope processes.value: Appointment and termination lifecycle: initial appointment on first application, agency and sub-producer appointments, voluntary terminations, terminations for cause, and the reporting of cause terminations to the state

In-scope systems.value: NIPR Gateway appointment and termination transactions, with statuses written back into the agency/producer management system that drives portal access and commission eligibility

Compliance procedure documented.value: Appointment & Termination Processing Procedure — per-state window table, first-application trigger capture, transaction submission and rejection handling, cause determination and reporting, and the downstream access and commission shut-off

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Producer Compliance Manager with Regulatory Counsel sign-off on the cause-termination reporting section; reviewed annually and on any state bulletin changing an appointment or termination window

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Event-driven — appointment must be submitted inside the state's window running from the date the first application was submitted (commonly 15 days from the application date in appointment-required states); termination notice must be filed inside the state's window (commonly 30 days from the termination effective date), with cause detail typically due to the producer within 15 days of the state filing

Deadline reminders configured.value: Case alerts fire at day 5 and day 10 of a 15-day appointment window and at day 15 and day 25 of a 30-day termination window, with a daily aged-transaction queue reported to the Distribution Operations Manager

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: NIPR transaction confirmations and reference numbers, the first-application trigger record, termination notices and cause files, and the producer notification letters retained 7 years after the appointment ends

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Every appointment or termination submitted outside the state window is logged with the state, day count over, the producer's NPN, the business written in the gap and the late-fee or penalty incurred

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every late transaction remediation, every cause determination and every decision not to report a termination as for cause

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All appointment and termination transactions submitted in the period from the NIPR transaction log, joined to their trigger events — first application date for appointments, termination effective date for terminations

Pass/fail thresholds.value: 95% of transactions submitted inside the state window; any transaction more than 30 days late, and any for-cause termination not reported as such, is an individual fail regardless of the aggregate rate

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is event-driven; the deadline dashboard is monitored daily by Licensing Ops and independent testing runs quarterly over the period's full transaction population

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not process appointment or termination transactions and must not have submitted any sampled transaction

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly appointment/termination timeliness workpaper (NIPR transaction extract, trigger reconciliation, day-count recomputation, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository under Distribution Compliance

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Per-state appointment and termination register with NIPR reference numbers, trigger dates, submission dates and computed day counts — producible for a market conduct exam appointment interrogatory within 10 business days

Regulator response path.value: Producer Compliance Manager answers state DOI appointment enquiries and pays any late-filing fee; Regulatory Counsel clears any cause-termination narrative before it is filed, given the defamation exposure and the statutory immunity conditions

checklist.step: Build and maintain the per-state appointment and termination window table
actions: For every state the entity is authorised in, record whether appointment is required at all, whether it is required before or after the first application, the number of days allowed from the trigger, and the appointment fee.
Record the termination window in days, whether the state requires a reason code, and whether a separate notice to the producer is required and within how many days.
Cite the statute or NIPR business rule for each cell so the number is defensible, and date the entry.
Re-read the table each quarter against state bulletins and NIPR rule updates and version the change with the date it takes effect.
checklist.done: every authorised state has a dated, cited appointment window, termination window and producer-notice requirement in the table.

checklist.step: Capture the first-application trigger the moment it happens
actions: Configure the policy administration system so the first application submitted by an unappointed producer in a state writes a trigger event with producer NPN, state, application number and submission date.
Push the trigger into the licensing queue in near real time — the clock in appointment-on-application states starts at the application date, not at the day Licensing notices.
Include applications taken through the Broker & Agent Portal and through any MGA or coverholder feed.
Reconcile the trigger feed to new-business counts weekly so a silent feed failure cannot burn the window.
checklist.done: every first application by an unappointed producer creates a dated trigger in the licensing queue, and the feed is reconciled weekly.

checklist.step: Confirm licence status before submitting the appointment
actions: Pull a current PDB report for the NPN and confirm the licence in the appointing state is Active with the lines the appointment will cover.
Check the eligibility record in the producer management system shows Eligible for that state and line and carries no restriction.
Where the licence is inactive or the line missing, hold the appointment and notify the Agency Relations Manager the same day — the application cannot be worked to bind.
Record the PDB reference used on the appointment case.
checklist.done: an active licence and matching lines are evidenced for the appointing state before submission.

checklist.step: Submit the appointment transaction through NIPR Gateway
actions: In NIPR Gateway open Appointments and start a new appointment, selecting the appointing company by NAIC co-code and the state.
Enter the producer NPN, the appointment type (individual or firm) and the lines of authority to be appointed.
Confirm the funding account has sufficient balance for the state appointment fee before submitting — an underfunded batch rejects silently and burns days.
Submit, capture the transaction reference number and submission date, and attach the confirmation to the appointment case.
checklist.done: the appointment is submitted with a captured NIPR reference number and confirmed fee payment.

checklist.step: Work rejections and pending statuses to closure inside the window
actions: Review the NIPR transaction status report daily and list every appointment in Rejected, Pending or Error status.
Read the rejection reason — mismatched NPN, missing line, licence not active, fee shortfall, company not authorised for the line — and fix the specific cause.
Resubmit and record both the original and resubmission dates; the state window runs from the trigger, not from the resubmission, so escalate any item where resubmission will land outside it.
Escalate items unresolved after 3 business days to the Producer Compliance Manager.
checklist.done: no appointment sits in Rejected or Error status for more than 3 business days without escalation, and each fix is recorded.

checklist.step: Write the confirmed appointment back into the downstream systems
actions: On NIPR confirmation, set the appointment status, state, lines and effective date on the producer record.
Release the state in the producer's portal territory and enable commission eligibility for that state and line in the commission platform.
Notify the Agency Relations Manager and the producer that they are appointed in the state, with the effective date.
Confirm the pending application that triggered the appointment can now be progressed and inform New Business.
checklist.done: the appointment is reflected in the producer record, portal territory and commission eligibility, and the triggering application is released.

checklist.step: Take the termination request and classify the reason
actions: Take the termination request from Distribution, HR or Compliance with the requested effective date and the underlying facts.

Classify it: voluntary (producer resigned or contract not renewed), administrative (no production, licence lapsed) or for cause (fraud, misappropriation of premium, forgery, misrepresentation, unlicensed activity, felony conviction).
For any suspected cause termination, open a documented file with the investigation findings, dates, amounts and the evidence relied on before the classification is fixed.
Route every proposed cause classification to Regulatory Counsel for clearance before the state filing is drafted.
checklist.done: the termination is classified with a written reason and, where for cause, an evidenced investigation file cleared by counsel.

checklist.step: Submit the termination transaction inside the state window
actions: In NIPR Gateway open Appointments ▸ Terminations, select the company and state, and enter the producer NPN.
Enter the termination effective date and select the state's reason code — the code must match the classification, and a cause termination coded as voluntary is itself a reporting failure.
Submit inside the state's window (commonly 30 days from the effective date) and capture the transaction reference.
Repeat per state; a producer terminated nationally needs a transaction in every state where an appointment exists.
checklist.done: a termination transaction with the correct reason code and a captured reference exists for every state of appointment, inside the window.

checklist.step: Send the producer the required termination notice
actions: Draft the notice to the producer stating the termination, its effective date and, where the state requires it, a copy of the information filed with the Commissioner.
Send it within the state's window (commonly 15 days of the state filing) by the method the state requires, keeping proof of despatch.
Use the counsel-cleared wording for cause terminations so the statutory immunity for good-faith reporting is preserved.
File the notice and the despatch proof in the document repository against the producer record.
checklist.done: a dated notice with proof of despatch is on file for every termination where the state requires producer notice.

checklist.step: Shut off access, authority and commission on the effective date
actions: Disable the producer's portal login and quoting rights effective the termination date and confirm no open quotes remain in their name.
Withdraw any binding authority or delegated authority letter and notify the Delegated Authority Manager where a binder is involved.
Set the commission platform to stop new-business commission and apply the renewal/vesting treatment the producer agreement specifies for the termination reason.
Reassign the in-force book to a servicing producer and write to affected policyholders where the agreement or the state requires it.
checklist.done: access, authority and new-business commission are stopped on the effective date and the book is reassigned.

checklist.step: Report cause terminations to the state and to any onward enquirer correctly
actions: Confirm the state filing contains the facts required — what happened, when, amounts involved — without opinion or characterisation beyond the evidence.
Keep the supporting investigation file intact and legally privileged where applicable, and ready for a Commissioner request.
Set the standing answer for future reference requests from other carriers so it matches the state filing exactly.
Record the counsel clearance date and the filing reference on the termination case.
checklist.done: the cause filing is factually supported, counsel-cleared and consistent with the standing reference answer.

checklist.step: Run the daily aged-transaction dashboard
actions: Publish a dashboard showing every open appointment trigger and termination request with state, window length, days elapsed and days remaining.
Colour anything inside 5 days of its deadline red and route it to the named Licensing Ops owner.
Show the count of transactions submitted late in the rolling 90 days against the 95% timeliness target.
Review the dashboard in the daily Licensing Ops stand-up and record the actions taken on red items.
checklist.done: the dashboard is published daily, red items have named owners, and the rolling timeliness rate is visible against target.

checklist.step: Remediate late and missed transactions
actions: For each transaction submitted outside the window, compute the days late from the trigger date and record the business written by that producer in the gap.
Submit the transaction immediately regardless of lateness and pay any state late fee, recording the payment reference.
Raise a tracker issue with root cause — trigger feed gap, rejection not worked, fee shortfall, misclassified reason — and an owner.
Where business was written while unappointed in an appointment-required state, refer to Regulatory Counsel for the notification and commission-treatment decision.
checklist.done: every late transaction is submitted, day-counted, fee-paid where due, and carries a tracked root cause and owner.

checklist.step: Reconcile the transaction log to the state records monthly
actions: Download the NIPR appointment report for the company by state and compare it to the appointment status held in the producer management system.

Investigate every producer appointed at the state but not in the internal system (unbilled appointment fees) and every producer active internally but not appointed at the state (unappointed production risk).
Correct the internal record or submit the missing transaction within 5 business days of the reconciliation.
Sign and file the monthly reconciliation with its difference schedule.
checklist.done: a signed monthly reconciliation with a cleared difference schedule exists between NIPR state records and the internal appointment register.

checklist.step: File the appointment and termination evidence
actions: File per producer per state: trigger record, PDB check, NIPR transaction confirmation with reference and date, termination notice with despatch proof and any cause file reference.
Store under Distribution Compliance / Appointments / <state> / <NPN>.
Apply the 7-years-after-appointment-end retention label.
Confirm retrieval by NPN, state, transaction type and date range works.
checklist.done: every transaction has a filed, retention-labelled evidence set retrievable by NPN, state and date.

testing.step: Build the transaction population from the source of record
actions: Download the NIPR transaction history for the company for the period: all appointment and termination transactions with NPN, state, type, reason code, submission date and status.
Add the internal appointment and termination case log so transactions that were never submitted appear in the population.
Reconcile the two counts and list every internal case with no NIPR transaction and every NIPR transaction with no internal case.
testing.done: the population reconciles NIPR transactions to internal cases with both directions of difference listed.

testing.step: Reconcile appointments to their first-application trigger
actions: Extract every first application submitted in the period by producer and state from the policy administration system, including portal and MGA feeds.
Join to appointment transactions on NPN + state and identify applications with no appointment at all.
For matched pairs, carry the application date forward as the trigger date for the day-count test.
Quantify premium written by producers with no appointment in appointment-required states.
testing.done: every first application in an appointment-required state is matched to an appointment or listed with premium quantified.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of for-cause terminations and 100% of transactions the internal log already flags as late.
Take 40 transactions at random with a recorded seed, stratified across appointment versus termination and across the five highest-volume states.
Record population size, strata, seed and draw date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, includes all cause terminations and known-late items, and its method is documented.

testing.step: Re-derive the statutory window for each sampled state
actions: For each sampled state, read the producer licensing statute and the current NIPR business rule and state the appointment and termination windows independently of the internal table.
Compare to the internal window table cell and its cited source; a stale or wrong cell invalidates every day-count computed from it.
Note whether the window runs in calendar or business days and from which event — application date, first commission, or effective date.
Record the re-derived window and its source in the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled state's window is independently re-derived, sourced, and compared to the internal table.

testing.step: Recompute the day count on every sampled transaction
actions: Compute days elapsed = submission date minus trigger date for each sampled transaction using the re-derived day convention.
Compare to the window and mark each transaction on-time or late with the number of days over.
Recompute the aggregate timeliness rate for the period and compare it to the 95% threshold and to the rate the dashboard reported.
Flag any transaction more than 30 days late as an individual fail regardless of the aggregate.
testing.done: every sampled transaction has an independently recomputed day count, and the aggregate rate is compared to both the threshold and the reported rate.

testing.step: Trace each sampled transaction to its NIPR confirmation
actions: Search the recorded NIPR reference number in the Gateway transaction history and confirm it exists for the right company, NPN, state and type.
Confirm the final status is Completed rather than Pending, Rejected or Error, and read the effective date the state recorded.
Compare the state-recorded effective date to the date held internally and to the date access and commission were actually switched.
Screenshot the transaction detail into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled transaction resolves to a completed NIPR record whose effective date matches the internal record.

testing.step: Re-perform the cause classification on sampled terminations
actions: Read the investigation file behind each sampled termination and reach an independent classification before reading the one recorded.
Test specifically for terminations coded voluntary or administrative where the file shows misappropriation of premium, forgery, unlicensed activity or misrepresentation.
Confirm the reason code submitted to the state matches the classification and that counsel clearance is dated before the filing.
A for-cause fact pattern reported as voluntary is a reportable failure, not a coding error.
testing.done: each sampled termination's classification is independently re-performed and reconciled to the reason code filed.

testing.step: Test the producer notice and the downstream shut-off
actions: For each sampled termination in a notice state, confirm a notice exists, read its despatch date, and recompute it against the state's notice window from the filing date.
Check the portal access removal date and the commission stop date against the termination effective date.
Extract any policy submitted or commission paid to the producer after the effective date and quantify it.
Confirm binding or delegated authority was formally withdrawn where one existed.
testing.done: notice timeliness is recomputed and no access, submission or new-business commission survives the effective date without being quantified.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, exposure and owner
actions: Raise one issue per exception with NPN, state, transaction type, days late, business written in the gap and any state fee incurred.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list: trigger feed gap, rejection not worked, fee funding shortfall, wrong reason code, notice not sent, access not removed.
Assign an owner and remediation date, and refer misreported cause terminations to Regulatory Counsel for correction with the state.
Carry open issues into the next quarterly test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with day count, exposure, root cause, owner, remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compare the recomputed timeliness rate to the 95% threshold and list every individual fail over 30 days late and every misclassified cause termination.
State the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper reference behind each figure.
Have the independent reviewer, who processed none of the sampled transactions, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Distribution Compliance forum with the state-level late schedule and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with the recomputed timeliness rate, individual fails, conclusion and reporting date is filed in the repository.
