checklist.step: Build the rolling renewal calendar from PDB expiry data
actions: Run the monthly PDB bulk report for all appointed producers and extract licence expiry dates by state and licence class.
Load expiries into the renewal calendar with producer NPN, state, resident/non-resident flag, class and days to expiry.
Flag producers whose resident licence expiry drives dependent non-resident renewals — a lapsed resident licence collapses the non-resident licences behind it.
Reconcile the calendar count to the appointed-producer count and investigate any producer with no expiry date returned.
checklist.done: the calendar holds a dated expiry row for every appointed producer and state, reconciled to the appointed population.

checklist.step: Publish the per-state CE requirement table
actions: For each state record the total CE hours per renewal cycle, the ethics hours included, and any line-specific mandates such as annuity suitability training or long-term care training.
Record whether non-resident producers are exempt on reciprocity and which state's credits satisfy the requirement.
Cite the state statute or DOI education page for each cell and date the entry.
Refresh the table quarterly and version any change with its effective date so a mid-cycle change is visible.
checklist.done: each state has a dated, cited CE requirement row covering total hours, ethics hours and line-specific mandates.

checklist.step: Set the EU continuing professional training plan
actions: Assign every EU intermediary and every employee involved in distribution a CPD plan totalling at least 15 hours for the calendar year, per IDD Art. 10(2).

Build the plan from the Annex I areas relevant to the products they distribute: terms and conditions, applicable law, claims and complaints handling, conflicts of interest, and for IBIP sellers the financial-competence and suitability modules under Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/2359.
Set the LMS to count only completed, assessed modules toward the 15 hours and to record duration per module.
Publish each person's plan and running hours on their LMS profile so the shortfall is visible to them and their manager.
checklist.done: every distribution-facing person has a 15-hour plan mapped to Annex I areas with running completed hours visible on their profile.

checklist.step: Fire the staged renewal reminders
actions: Configure the reminder engine to email the producer and copy the Agency Relations Manager at 120, 90, 60 and 30 days before each licence expiry.
Include in the reminder: state, licence number, expiry date, CE hours still required, and the direct NIPR renewal link.
Escalate to the Head of Distribution any producer with an in-force book still unrenewed at 30 days.
Log every reminder sent against the producer record so non-response is provable.
checklist.done: reminders are logged at each of the four stages for every expiring licence, with 30-day escalations recorded.

checklist.step: Compute the CE gap per producer per state
actions: Pull the CE transcript for each producer from the state education vendor (Sircon or the state's CE provider) by NPN and cycle.
Compare banked credits to the state requirement, splitting general hours, ethics hours and any line-specific mandate separately — a producer can be over on general hours and still fail on ethics.
Compute hours still required and the last safe completion date, allowing 10 business days for the education provider to report credits to the state.
Publish the shortfall list weekly to producers, agency managers and the Head of Distribution.
checklist.done: each producer has a computed shortfall by credit category with a last safe completion date, published weekly.

checklist.step: Book and deliver the courses that close the gap
actions: Match each shortfall to state-approved courses, checking the course's approval number is valid for the state and credit category.
Enrol the producer, set a completion date at least 15 business days before licence expiry, and confirm the provider will report the credits to the state.
For annuity and long-term care mandates, book the specific state-approved product training rather than generic hours.
Chase non-completion at 5 business days before the internal completion date and escalate to the agency manager.
checklist.done: every shortfall has enrolled, state-approved courses with completion dates set ahead of expiry and chased to completion.

checklist.step: Confirm credits have posted to the state before renewing
actions: Re-pull the CE transcript after the course completion date and confirm the state shows the credits banked — a completion certificate in hand is not a banked credit.
Where credits have not posted within 10 business days, contact the education provider with the course approval number and completion date and record the chase.
Only mark the producer renewal-ready when the state transcript satisfies every credit category.
Record the transcript date relied on.
checklist.done: the state CE transcript, not the certificate, evidences full compliance before the renewal is submitted.

checklist.step: Submit the renewal transaction and pay the fee
actions: In NIPR Gateway open Licensing ▸ Renewal for the state and enter the NPN and licence number.
Answer the background and disclosure questions consistently with the producer's record — a new criminal or regulatory matter here routes back to the §1033 screening before the renewal goes in.
Pay the state renewal fee and any transaction fee from the funded account and capture the confirmation reference.
Attach the confirmation to the producer record and update the new expiry date in the renewal calendar.
checklist.done: the renewal is submitted with fee paid, the confirmation reference captured and the new expiry loaded into the calendar.

checklist.step: Verify the renewed status in the PDB
actions: Pull a fresh PDB report 5 business days after submission and confirm status Active with the new expiry date and unchanged lines of authority.
Investigate any line dropped at renewal — some states drop a line where its specific CE mandate was unmet — and reinstate it before the producer sells that product.
Update the producer record and the portal product catalogue to match the renewed lines.
File the fresh PDB report as renewal evidence.
checklist.done: a post-renewal PDB report evidences Active status, the new expiry and the retained lines, with any dropped line addressed.

checklist.step: Suspend selling rights the moment a licence lapses
actions: Set the system to flip the producer's state eligibility to Suspended automatically at 00:01 on the day after expiry when no renewal is confirmed.
Remove the state from the producer's portal territory and block new submissions and quotes in that state.
Stop new-business commission for that state in the commission platform pending reinstatement.
Notify the producer, the agency manager and New Business the same day, and reassign any pending applications.
checklist.done: expired licences suspend selling rights automatically on the day after expiry with all parties notified and pending work reassigned.

checklist.step: Run the reinstatement path for lapsed licences
actions: Read the state's reinstatement rules: the grace period during which a late renewal with penalty is accepted, and the date after which a full new licence application and possibly re-examination is required.
Where inside the grace period, submit the late renewal with the penalty fee and record both the date and the amount.
Where outside it, open a new licence application, and treat the producer as unlicensed for the whole intervening period.
Record the lapse start and end dates on the producer record — they define the exposure window for any business written.
checklist.done: each lapse has the correct reinstatement route executed and a recorded lapse start and end date.

checklist.step: Quantify and remediate business written during a lapse
actions: Extract every application, bind and renewal by the producer between the lapse start and end dates, with premium and commission.
Freeze commission on that business and quantify the amount for the clawback or state-specific handling decision.
Refer the population to Regulatory Counsel for the decision on state notification, policy validity and any customer communication.
Log the exposure in the tracker with root cause and remediation owner.
checklist.done: business written during each lapse is extracted, quantified, commission-frozen and referred for a counsel decision.

checklist.step: Close and evidence the EU CPD year
actions: At 31 December, run the CPD ledger for every distribution-facing person and list total assessed hours against the 15-hour minimum, broken down by Annex I area.
Chase anyone under target through their manager with a documented catch-up plan, and record the shortfall as an exception regardless of catch-up.
Generate a per-person annual CPD statement showing modules, dates, durations and assessment outcomes, and have the person and their manager acknowledge it.
Send the aggregate result to the Head of Compliance for the Art. 10 competence attestation.
checklist.done: every distribution-facing person has a signed annual CPD statement and the aggregate 15-hour position is reported to Compliance.

checklist.step: Report renewal and CE performance to Distribution and Compliance
actions: Publish a monthly view: licences expiring in the next 120 days, renewal-on-time rate against the 98% target, open CE shortfalls, live lapses and business exposed by lapse.
Break the view by agency and channel so persistent offenders are visible to the Head of Distribution.
Take the lapse and CPD-shortfall items to the Distribution Compliance forum with named owners and dates.
Record the forum decisions against the tracker issues.
checklist.done: a monthly renewal and CE report with on-time rate, lapses and exposure is published and taken to the compliance forum with owned actions.

checklist.step: File the renewal and CE evidence
actions: File per producer per cycle: CE transcript, course certificates with approval numbers, renewal confirmation and reference, post-renewal PDB report, and any lapse and reinstatement records.
File per EU intermediary per year: the annual CPD statement and its module ledger.
Store under Distribution Compliance / Renewals / <year> / <NPN> and apply the 7-years-after-cycle-end retention label.
Confirm retrieval by NPN, state, cycle year and expiry date works.
checklist.done: renewal, CE and CPD evidence is filed per cycle, retention-labelled and retrievable by NPN and cycle year.

testing.step: Build the population of licences expiring and CPD years closing
actions: Pull an independent PDB bulk extract of all appointed producers with licence expiry dates falling in the test period, by state and class.
Add every EU intermediary and distribution-facing employee whose 15-hour CPD year closed in the period.
Reconcile the extract to the internal renewal calendar and list producers present in one and not the other.
testing.done: the population is built from an independent PDB extract and reconciled to the internal renewal calendar in both directions.

testing.step: Reconcile every expiry to a renewal or a recorded lapse
actions: For each expiry, confirm either a renewal confirmed on or before the expiry date, or a lapse record with a start date matching the day after expiry.
Flag expiries with neither — those are undetected lapses and the most serious finding available here.
Compute the renewal-on-time rate for the period and compare it to the 98% threshold and to the rate management reported.
List every producer with an in-force book among the lapses.
testing.done: every expiry resolves to an on-time renewal or a recorded lapse, with the on-time rate recomputed and undetected lapses listed.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of lapses, 100% of late renewals and 100% of EU CPD shortfalls.
Take 40 renewals at random with a recorded seed, stratified across resident and non-resident licences and across the states with line-specific CE mandates.
Record population size, strata, seed and draw date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all lapses, late renewals and CPD shortfalls, and its method is documented.

testing.step: Re-derive the CE requirement for each sampled state
actions: Open each sampled state's DOI continuing-education page and statute and state the total hours, ethics hours and line-specific mandates independently of the internal table.
Compare to the internal CE requirement table cell and its citation; a stale cell invalidates every gap computed from it.
Check whether the state grants non-resident reciprocity and whether the internal table applied it correctly.
Record the re-derived requirement and source in the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled state's CE requirement is independently re-derived, sourced and compared to the internal table.

testing.step: Re-perform the CE transcript check against the state record
actions: Pull the sampled producer's CE transcript directly from the state education vendor on the test date, not from the file copy.
Recompute banked credits by category against the re-derived requirement and confirm the requirement was satisfied on or before the licence expiry date.
Check each course's state approval number was valid for that state and credit category on the completion date.
Credits banked after expiry are an individual fail even where the state later accepted the renewal.
testing.done: each sampled producer's credits are recomputed from the state transcript and shown banked before expiry, or the fail is logged.

testing.step: Trace renewals to NIPR confirmations and post-renewal status
actions: Search each sampled renewal reference in NIPR Gateway and confirm it exists for the right NPN, state and licence class.
Read the transaction date and the new expiry date and compare both to the internal record.
Pull a current PDB report and confirm status Active and that no line of authority silently dropped at renewal.
Screenshot the transaction and PDB detail into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled renewal traces to a completed NIPR transaction and a currently Active PDB status with lines intact.

testing.step: Recompute the EU 15-hour CPD position
actions: Export the LMS module ledger for each sampled person for the closed calendar year with module names, dates, durations and assessment outcomes.
Sum only completed and assessed modules and compare the total to the 15-hour minimum — count no in-progress or unassessed activity.
Check the mix covers the Annex I areas relevant to the products the person actually sold in the year, including the IBIP modules where they sold IBIPs.
Any person under 15 hours, or over 15 hours but missing a relevant Annex I area, is an individual fail.
testing.done: each sampled person's assessed CPD hours and Annex I coverage are independently recomputed against the 15-hour minimum.

testing.step: Test the lapse suspension control and quantify exposure
actions: For each lapse, confirm the eligibility flag flipped to Suspended on the day after expiry and that portal access and commission were stopped that day.
Extract every application, bind, renewal and commission payment by the producer inside the lapse window and quantify premium and commission.
Compare the quantified exposure to what Compliance recorded — an understated exposure is itself an exception.
Confirm a Regulatory Counsel decision on notification and policy treatment exists for every lapse with business written.
testing.done: every lapse shows same-day suspension, an independently quantified exposure and a counsel decision where business was written.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, exposure and owner
actions: Raise one issue per exception with NPN, state, expiry date, days lapsed, credits short by category, and premium and commission exposed.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list: expiry not on calendar, reminders not actioned, credits booked too late to post, wrong CE requirement applied, suspension control failed, CPD plan not assigned.
Assign an owner and remediation date, and refer lapse-period business to Regulatory Counsel.
Carry open issues into the next semi-annual test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with day counts, credit shortfall, exposure, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compare the recomputed renewal-on-time rate to the 98% threshold, count lapses on producers with in-force books against the zero threshold, and count CPD shortfalls.
State the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper reference behind each figure.
Have the independent reviewer, who owns neither the renewal calendar nor the CPD curriculum, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Distribution Compliance forum and provide the Art. 10 competence position to the Head of Compliance, then file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with the on-time rate, lapse count, CPD position, conclusion and reporting date is filed in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the pre-engagement fitness screen for every person who will conduct the business of insurance — 18 U.S.C. §1033 prohibited-person determination and the IDD Art. 10(3) good-repute assessment — and holds the authority to refuse an engagement

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — IDD (EU) 2016/97 Art. 17(1) (honest, fair, professional conduct) with Art. 10(3) good repute, re-read on EUR-Lex; the US leg re-read against 18 U.S.C. §§1033-1034 (prohibition on persons convicted of a felony involving dishonesty or breach of trust engaging in the business of insurance without written consent) and the acting state's §1033 consent-waiver procedure

In-scope processes.value: Pre-engagement fitness screening for employees in insurance functions, producers and sub-producers, MGA and coverholder staff with binding authority, and TPA claims handlers — plus re-screening on any new conviction, regulatory action or role change into a licensable function

In-scope systems.value: HRIS holds the employee screening status and hire gate; the agency/producer management system holds the producer equivalent; background results come from the screening vendor and Credit Bureau & Data Services and are stored in the compliance evidence repository, never in the HR record

Compliance procedure documented.value: Fitness & Propriety Screening Procedure — role scoping against the 'business of insurance' test, consent and FCRA disclosure, criminal and regulatory searches, §1033 prohibited-person determination, 1033 written-consent waiver application where a conviction exists, EU good-repute assessment, adverse-action process and re-screening triggers

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance with Employment Counsel sign-off on the consent, adverse-action and record-handling sections; reviewed annually and on any change to state consent-waiver procedure or FCRA/GDPR handling

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per hire and per producer engagement — screening must complete before the start date or first solicitation; a §1033 written-consent application must be filed with the acting state before the person performs any insurance function, and self-disclosure of a new qualifying conviction is required immediately on notification

Deadline reminders configured.value: Requisition-level alerts at offer stage and 5 days before start date for any incomplete screen, plus an annual self-attestation campaign reminder and an immediate alert when a NIPR regulatory-action feed or an HR disciplinary case raises a new conviction

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Signed consent and disclosure forms, the screening report, the §1033 determination memo, any state consent-waiver application and grant, and the good-repute assessment retained 7 years after the engagement ends, in the compliance evidence repository with restricted access

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any person who started in an insurance function before the screen cleared, and any prohibited person found performing insurance functions without a written consent waiver, is logged with the dates worked, the functions performed and the removal or waiver action taken

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every §1033 prohibited-person determination, every decision to sponsor a consent-waiver application, and every removal or continued engagement following an adverse finding

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All hires, internal transfers into insurance functions, and producer or coverholder engagements commenced in the period, plus everyone flagged by the annual self-attestation or by a new regulatory action during the period

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — any start in an insurance function without a completed screen, and any prohibited person engaged without a written consent waiver, is an individual fail escalated to the Head of Compliance within one business day

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per hire and per engagement; testing runs quarterly over that quarter's joiners and engagements, plus 100% review of every case where a conviction or regulatory action was disclosed

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside Compliance screening and HR recruitment and must not have made any sampled determination

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly fitness-screening test workpaper (joiner and engagement population, screen completion dates, determination re-performance, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository under restricted access

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Per-person screening file — consent, search results, §1033 determination memo, waiver application and grant, good-repute assessment — producible for a DOI market conduct interrogatory or an NCA fitness review within 10 business days, redacted per data-protection rules

Regulator response path.value: Head of Compliance answers DOI and NCA fitness enquiries; Employment Counsel and Regulatory Counsel jointly clear any disclosure of an individual's conviction data before release, and Regulatory Counsel decides on any state notification

checklist.step: Scope which roles fall inside the business of insurance
actions: List every job family and every distributor arrangement and mark whether the holder engages in the business of insurance — underwriting, claims handling, producing, premium handling, policy administration, actuarial and compliance functions all do; unrelated facilities or catering roles do not.
Include contractors, MGA and coverholder staff with binding authority, and TPA claims handlers — 18 U.S.C. §1033 attaches to the activity, not the employment contract.
Add every EU distribution-facing role for the Art. 10(3) good-repute test, including management responsible for distribution.
Publish the scoped role list to the HR Business Partner and the Recruiter Talent Acquisition Specialist so requisitions carry the screening flag automatically.
checklist.done: a published role list marks every in-scope job family and distributor arrangement, and requisitions inherit the screening flag.

checklist.step: Attach the screening gate to the requisition and the engagement
actions: Set the screening requirement field on every in-scope requisition at creation so it flows to the offer stage.
Configure the applicant tracking workflow so an offer cannot move to 'Accepted — start date confirmed' while the screening status is Pending.
Mirror the same gate on producer and coverholder onboarding cases in the producer management system.
Report weekly to the Compliance Officer any requisition or onboarding case where the gate was overridden and by whom.
checklist.done: no in-scope offer or engagement can be confirmed while the screening status is Pending, and overrides are reported weekly.

checklist.step: Take lawful consent and give the required disclosures
actions: Issue the standalone background-check disclosure and written authorisation for signature — kept as its own document, not buried in the application form, as FCRA requires.
For EU candidates issue the data-protection notice covering the lawful basis for processing criminal-conviction data and the retention period, and take the specific consent the local law requires.

Collect the candidate's self-disclosure form: any felony conviction involving dishonesty or breach of trust, any insurance-related regulatory action, any pending charge, and any prior licence refusal, suspension or revocation.
Route signed consents into the compliance evidence repository, not the general HR file, and record only the completion status in the HRIS.
checklist.done: a signed standalone consent, the data-protection notice where applicable, and a completed self-disclosure form are on file before any search runs.

checklist.step: Run the criminal and identity searches
actions: Order from the screening vendor: identity and right-to-work verification, county and federal criminal searches for every jurisdiction of residence in the last 7 years, national criminal database, and the sex-offender and global sanctions checks.
For EU candidates order the equivalent national criminal-record certificate the home state requires for Art. 10(3), and an undischarged-bankruptcy check.
Specify a scope that returns the offence, the statute, the disposition and the date — a 'record found' flag with no detail cannot support a §1033 determination.
Log the order date and the vendor reference on the screening case and chase anything outstanding after 5 business days.
checklist.done: criminal, identity and sanctions searches are ordered with detail-level results and their vendor references logged.

checklist.step: Run the insurance-specific regulatory and licensing searches
actions: For anyone who holds or will hold a licence, pull the PDB report and read the Regulatory Actions section for every state.
Search the NAIC Regulatory Information Retrieval System and the acting state's DOI enforcement orders page by name.
For EU intermediaries search the home Member State register and the EIOPA register for any withdrawal or restriction of registration.
Record every hit with state, date, allegation, disposition and sanction on the screening case.
checklist.done: regulatory and licensing history is searched across PDB, state enforcement records and EU registers, with every hit recorded.

checklist.step: Make the §1033 prohibited-person determination
actions: For each criminal record returned, apply the §1033(e) test in writing: was the offence a felony, and did it involve dishonesty or breach of trust, or was it a violation of §1033 itself.
Read the charging document or the judgment rather than the vendor summary where the offence classification is not obvious — a misdemeanour plea to a felony charge changes the answer.
Record the determination — Not prohibited / Prohibited, consent required — with the offence, statute, date, jurisdiction and the reasoning behind it.
Route every Prohibited determination to the Head of Compliance and Employment Counsel the same day.
checklist.done: each criminal record has a written §1033 determination citing the offence, statute and reasoning, with prohibited cases escalated same day.

checklist.step: Make the IDD Art. 10(3) good-repute assessment
actions: Assess whether the person has a clean criminal record or other national equivalent in relation to serious criminal offences linked to crimes against property or financial activity.
Confirm the person has not previously been declared bankrupt, unless rehabilitated in accordance with national law.
For management responsible for distribution, assess the wider fitness evidence — prior regulatory findings, dismissals for conduct, unresolved complaints — and record the conclusion.
Write the assessment into the case with its evidence references; a bare 'no adverse findings' with no searches behind it is not an assessment.
checklist.done: a written good-repute assessment covering criminal record, bankruptcy and conduct history, with evidence references, is on the case.

checklist.step: Run the pre-adverse and adverse action process where a finding blocks the engagement
actions: Issue the pre-adverse action notice with a copy of the consumer report and the summary of rights, and allow the statutory response period before any decision is finalised.
Consider the individual assessment factors — nature and gravity of the offence, time elapsed, relevance to the role — and record them.
Where the decision stands, issue the adverse action notice naming the consumer reporting agency and the person's dispute rights.
File the notices and the individualised assessment in the screening case.
checklist.done: every adverse decision has a pre-adverse notice, a recorded individualised assessment and an adverse action notice on file.

checklist.step: Sponsor a §1033 written consent waiver where the business case supports it
actions: Decide with the Head of Compliance whether to sponsor the person, and record the business rationale.

Prepare the acting state's 1033 consent application: the person's sworn statement, certified court records including the judgment and evidence of sentence completion, a letter of sponsorship from the employer, character references and a fidelity-bond confirmation where the state requires one.
File with the state Commissioner's licensing division per the state's published 1033 consent procedure and record the filing date and reference.
Keep the person out of any insurance function until the written consent is granted, and record the grant, its scope and any conditions on the case.
checklist.done: a filed consent application with a recorded state reference exists, and the person performs no insurance function before the written consent is granted.

checklist.step: Release the hire or engagement gate on a clear determination
actions: Set the HRIS screening status to Cleared with the determination date and the compliance case reference — never the underlying conviction detail.
Release the start date in onboarding and, for producers, release the eligibility flag in the producer management system.
Where the clearance is conditional — consent waiver granted with restrictions, supervision requirement — record the condition and configure the supervision.
Notify the hiring manager or the Agency Relations Manager that the person may commence.
checklist.done: the screening status, determination date and case reference are on the HRIS or producer record and the start is released.

checklist.step: Run the annual self-attestation across in-scope people
actions: Issue an annual attestation to everyone in an in-scope role asking them to confirm no new felony conviction involving dishonesty or breach of trust, no new pending charge and no new regulatory action since the last attestation.
Track completion and escalate non-responders to their manager at 10 business days and to the Head of Compliance at 20.
Route every positive disclosure into a fresh screening case the day it is received.
Report completion percentage and disclosure count to the Head of Compliance at campaign close.
checklist.done: the annual attestation reaches every in-scope person with completion tracked and every positive disclosure opened as a screening case.

checklist.step: Screen continuously on regulatory and conduct triggers
actions: Take the daily NIPR regulatory-action alert feed and open a re-screening case for any new action against an engaged producer.
Take from Employee Relations any disciplinary outcome involving dishonesty, and from SIU any internal fraud finding, and open a re-screening case.
Suspend the person's insurance functions pending the re-determination where the trigger is a felony charge or a licence suspension.
Record every trigger, its source and the re-determination outcome on the person's case.
checklist.done: every regulatory, disciplinary or fraud trigger opens a dated re-screening case with a recorded re-determination.

checklist.step: Remove prohibited persons from insurance functions
actions: Where a person is determined prohibited and no consent waiver is in place, remove them from all insurance functions immediately — system access, authority, claim and policy handling.
Extract the work they performed since the disqualifying date and hand it to the relevant function for review of any decision they made.
Decide with Regulatory Counsel whether a state notification or a producer termination-for-cause filing is required.
Record the removal date, the scope of the review and the counsel decision on the case.
checklist.done: prohibited persons are removed from insurance functions on determination, their work is reviewed, and the notification decision is recorded.

checklist.step: Protect the screening data
actions: Restrict the screening repository to the named Compliance and Employment Counsel group and log every access.
Confirm criminal-conviction data is held only in that repository and not copied into HRIS fields, email or shared drives.
Apply the 7-years-after-engagement-end retention rule and confirm automatic deletion is scheduled, tighter where local law requires it.
Include the screening processing in the record of processing activities with its lawful basis.
checklist.done: screening data is access-restricted, access-logged, held in one location and scheduled for deletion at the retention limit.

checklist.step: File the screening evidence pack
actions: File per person: signed consent and disclosures, self-disclosure form, search results, §1033 determination memo, good-repute assessment, any adverse-action notices, and any consent-waiver application and grant.
Store under Compliance / Fitness Screening / <year> / <person reference> with restricted access.
Apply the 7-years-after-engagement-end retention label.
Confirm retrieval by person reference, determination date and outcome works for an exam response.
checklist.done: each person's screening pack is filed under restricted access, retention-labelled and retrievable by reference and outcome.

testing.step: Build the population of joiners and engagements
actions: Extract every hire, rehire and internal transfer with a start date in the period, with job family, start date and location.
Add every producer, coverholder and TPA engagement commenced in the period from the producer management system and the contract repository.
Mark each row in-scope or out-of-scope by applying the published business-of-insurance role list independently, and challenge any role scoped out that handles premium, claims or policy decisions.
Reconcile the joiner count to payroll starts and the engagement count to new producer codes.
testing.done: the population covers employees, producers and third-party staff, is reconciled to payroll and producer codes, and scoping is independently applied.

testing.step: Reconcile every in-scope start to a completed screen
actions: Join the population to screening cases on person reference and confirm a determination dated on or before the start date or first solicitation.
List starts with no case, cases determined after the start date, and cases closed with no determination memo.
Compute days worked in an insurance function before the determination for each late case.
Treat every one as an automatic exception without judgement.
testing.done: every in-scope start is matched to a determination pre-dating it or is listed with the days worked unscreened.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of cases with any criminal record, regulatory action or positive self-disclosure, and 100% of consent-waiver cases.
Take 30 clear cases at random with a recorded seed, stratified across employees, producers and third-party staff.
Record population size, strata, seed and draw date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, includes every adverse and waiver case, and its method is documented.

testing.step: Test consent and disclosure validity
actions: For each sampled case read the authorisation and confirm the disclosure was a standalone document signed before the search date.
Compare the signature date to the vendor order date — a search run before consent is a legal defect, not a paperwork gap.
For EU candidates confirm the data-protection notice and the lawful basis for criminal-conviction processing are on file.
Confirm the self-disclosure form is complete and signed, with no blank questions.
testing.done: every sampled case has a valid standalone consent signed before the search and, for EU cases, a documented lawful basis.

testing.step: Verify search scope and completeness against the vendor record
actions: Pull the vendor's order detail for each sampled case and list the searches actually run.
Compare the jurisdictions searched to the person's declared address history for the last 7 years and flag any gap.
Confirm results returned offence, statute, disposition and date rather than a bare hit flag.
Confirm the licensing and regulatory searches were run for every licence-holding person, including the PDB pull.
testing.done: search scope covers the full address history and returns determination-grade detail for every sampled case.

testing.step: Re-perform the §1033 determination on adverse cases
actions: Read the charging document and judgment for each sampled criminal record and reach an independent §1033(e) conclusion before reading the recorded determination.
Test specifically for felonies involving dishonesty or breach of trust classified as not prohibited on thin reasoning, and for reliance on the vendor summary rather than the court record.
Compare to the recorded determination; a right answer supported by wrong or absent reasoning is still an exception.
Record the independent conclusion and its source documents in the workpaper.
testing.done: each adverse case carries an independent §1033 conclusion drawn from court records and compared to the recorded determination.

testing.step: Trace consent waivers to the state grant and its scope
actions: For each waiver case, obtain the filed application and the state's written consent grant with its date, reference and any conditions.
Compare the grant date to the date the person first performed an insurance function and quantify any gap.
Confirm the functions performed sit inside the scope and conditions of the granted consent, including any supervision requirement.
Confirm the grant covers each state in which the person actually operates — a consent from one state does not travel.
testing.done: every waiver case shows a dated state grant covering the functions and states actually performed, with any gap quantified.

testing.step: Test the hire gate and the continuous trigger controls
actions: Attempt to move a test in-scope offer to accepted with screening status Pending and record whether the system blocks it.
Pull the override log for the period and test every override against a documented Compliance approval.
Take 10 NIPR regulatory-action alerts from the period and confirm each opened a re-screening case within one business day.
Confirm suspension of insurance functions actually occurred for triggers involving a felony charge or licence suspension.
testing.done: the hire gate blocks pending screens, every override is approved, and sampled triggers opened cases and suspensions within the service level.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, exposure and owner
actions: Raise one issue per exception with the person reference, role, days worked unscreened, functions performed and the states affected.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list: role scoped out wrongly, gate overridden, consent defect, search scope gap, determination unsupported, waiver not obtained, trigger not worked.
Assign an owner and a remediation date, and refer any prohibited person found operating without consent to Regulatory Counsel for the removal and notification decision immediately.
Carry open issues into the next quarterly test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with days exposed, functions performed, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Count unscreened starts and unconsented prohibited persons against the zero-tolerance threshold and summarise determination-quality defects.
State the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper reference behind each finding.
Have the independent reviewer, who made none of the sampled determinations, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Risk & Compliance Committee, redacting individual conviction detail, and file the workpaper under restricted access in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed, appropriately redacted workpaper with counts, conclusion and committee reporting date is filed under restricted access.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the quarterly three-way reconciliation of the internal producer roster to NIPR state appointment records and to producers actually paid commission; unresolved breaks escalate to the Producer Compliance Manager

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Quarterly — extracts taken as at quarter end, reconciliation completed and signed within 20 business days of quarter end, and every break resolved or formally aged within 30 business days of the sign-off

checklist.step: Specify and freeze the three extracts
actions: Write the extract specification: producer master fields (NPN, name, status, writing entity, state, lines, appointment status, effective and termination dates), NIPR appointment report fields (company NAIC co-code, state, NPN, appointment status, effective date), commission ledger fields (producer code, NPN, state, policy count, premium, commission paid).
Fix the as-at date at the last calendar day of the quarter for all three so the match is like-for-like.
Name the owner of each extract — Licensing Ops, Licensing Ops via NIPR, and the Commission Analyst — and the due date at quarter end plus 5 business days.
Store the frozen extracts read-only with their generation timestamps.
checklist.done: three read-only extracts share a common as-at date, carry the specified fields and are timestamped.

checklist.step: Download the NIPR state appointment report
actions: In NIPR Gateway open the appointment reporting section and request the full appointment listing for each writing company by NAIC co-code.
Run it for every state in which the company holds a Certificate of Authority, including states with no current production — orphan appointments hide there.
Download in the delimited format and record the report generation date and record count.
Reconcile the record count to the prior quarter's count plus the net appointments and terminations processed in the quarter, and investigate the difference before matching.
checklist.done: a dated NIPR appointment listing exists for every writing entity and state, with its record count reconciled to the quarter's transaction activity.

checklist.step: Extract the internal producer master
actions: Extract every producer record with status Active or Suspended, plus any terminated in the quarter, with NPN, writing entity, state, lines and appointment status.
Include agency records and their sub-producers as separate rows so an agency appointment does not mask an unappointed individual.
Flag records with a missing or malformed NPN — they cannot be matched and are a break in their own right.
Hand the extract with its row count to the reconciliation owner.
checklist.done: the producer master extract covers active, suspended and quarter-terminated producers and agencies, with missing NPNs flagged.

checklist.step: Extract producers who actually produced or were paid
actions: Extract every producer code paid commission in the quarter, with NPN, writing entity, state of risk, policy count, written premium and commission amount.
Add producers with bound business but no commission yet paid from the policy administration system so timing does not hide production.
Split the extract by state of risk, not by producer home state — appointment is required where the risk sits.
Reconcile total commission in the extract to the general ledger commission expense for the quarter.
checklist.done: the production and commission extract is split by state of risk and reconciles to ledger commission expense.

checklist.step: Run the three-way match
actions: Join the three extracts on NPN + writing-entity NAIC co-code + state, treating NPN as the only reliable key and never matching on name.

Produce four result sets: fully matched; in production/commission but no state appointment; in state appointment but not in the internal master; in the internal master as appointed but with no state appointment record.
Report row counts for each set with the percentage of the roster they represent.
Publish the match workbook to the reconciliation owner with the join logic documented so it can be re-performed.
checklist.done: the match produces four documented result sets with counts and percentages and re-performable join logic.

checklist.step: Categorise every break
actions: Assign each break a category: unappointed production (highest severity), appointment never submitted, appointment rejected and not reworked, termination processed internally but not at the state, orphan state appointment on a departed producer, NPN data defect, or timing difference inside the state's window.
For unappointed production, attach the policy count, written premium and commission paid so severity is quantified, not asserted.
For orphan state appointments, attach the annual appointment fee being wasted so Finance can see the cost.
Set an owner and a target resolution date on every break at categorisation.
checklist.done: every break carries a category, a quantified impact and a named owner with a target date.

checklist.step: Resolve unappointed production immediately
actions: Confirm the producer's licence is active in the state with the right lines, then submit the appointment transaction the same day.
Compute the exposure window from the first application or bind date to the appointment effective date and record it.
Freeze further commission on the affected business pending the Regulatory Counsel decision on notification and commission treatment.
Where the licence is not active, suspend the producer in that state and reassign the in-force book.
checklist.done: every unappointed-production break has a same-day appointment or suspension, a computed exposure window and frozen commission.

checklist.step: Clear orphan state appointments
actions: For each state appointment with no active internal producer, confirm whether the producer left, moved agency or was never engaged.

Where the relationship has ended, submit the termination transaction with the correct reason code and record the reference — an appointment left open keeps the carrier answerable for that producer's conduct.
Where the producer is genuinely active but missing internally, create or reactivate the internal record rather than terminating at the state.
Report the annual appointment fees recovered by clearing orphans to Finance.
checklist.done: every orphan appointment is either terminated at the state or matched to a reactivated internal record, with fees recovered reported.

checklist.step: Fix the data defects that caused matchless rows
actions: For each missing, duplicated or malformed NPN, resolve the correct NPN from a PDB lookup and correct the producer master.
Merge duplicate producer records that split one person's production across two codes, keeping the audit trail of the merge.
Add a validation rule at record creation that rejects a producer record without a PDB-verified NPN.
Re-run the match on the corrected rows and confirm they land in the matched set.
checklist.done: NPN defects are corrected at source, duplicates merged, a creation-time validation rule is live, and corrected rows re-match.

checklist.step: Age and escalate unresolved breaks
actions: Publish the break ageing view weekly: category, owner, days open, quantified impact.
Escalate any break older than 30 business days to the Producer Compliance Manager and any unappointed-production break older than 5 business days to the Head of Compliance.
Report the trend in break counts by category across quarters so recurring root causes are visible.
Record the action taken on every escalated break.
checklist.done: breaks are aged and escalated weekly against the 5- and 30-day thresholds with recorded actions.

checklist.step: Feed root causes back into the appointment process
actions: Group the quarter's breaks by root cause — trigger feed gap, rejection not worked, termination not filed at state, data defect at onboarding — and count each.
Raise a process issue for any root cause appearing in two consecutive quarters, with an owner in Licensing Ops or Distribution.
Agree a control change for each — a new validation, a changed queue service level, an added reconciliation field — with a date.
Verify at the next quarter's reconciliation whether the count for that root cause fell.
checklist.done: each recurring root cause has a raised issue, an agreed control change and a next-quarter verification point.

checklist.step: Reconcile the appointment fee spend
actions: Compare the state appointment and renewal fees paid in the quarter per the ledger to the count of appointments confirmed in the NIPR report.
Investigate fees paid with no corresponding confirmed appointment and appointments confirmed with no fee posted.
Quantify fees attributable to orphan appointments cleared in the quarter as an avoided ongoing cost.
Sign the fee reconciliation and attach it to the roster reconciliation pack.
checklist.done: appointment fee spend reconciles to confirmed appointments with differences investigated and the reconciliation signed.

checklist.step: Sign the quarterly reconciliation certificate
actions: Review the match result counts, the break schedule with quantified impacts, and the resolution status of each break.
Confirm the unresolved break rate is below 1% of the roster and that no unappointed-production break remains open.
Approve in writing any break carried forward, stating the reason and the target date.
Sign and date the certificate within 20 business days of quarter end and circulate it to the Head of Compliance and the Head of Distribution.
checklist.done: a signed, dated certificate within 20 business days states the break rate, lists carried-forward breaks and their approvals.

checklist.step: Report the result to Distribution and Compliance governance
actions: Take to the Distribution Compliance forum: match rates, break counts by category, quantified unappointed-production exposure, orphan fees recovered and the trend across quarters.
Name the agencies and channels generating the most breaks so remediation lands on the source.
Record forum decisions and owners against the tracker issues.
Escalate to the Risk & Compliance Committee any quarter with unappointed production carrying material premium.
checklist.done: the quarterly result is reported with named channel owners and forum decisions recorded against tracker issues.

checklist.step: File the reconciliation pack
actions: Assemble the pack: three timestamped extracts, the match workbook with join logic, the break schedule with resolutions, the fee reconciliation and the signed certificate.
File under Distribution Compliance / Roster Reconciliation / <year> / <quarter>.
Apply the 7-years-from-reconciliation-date retention label.
Confirm retrieval by quarter, writing entity and state works for an exam response.
checklist.done: the quarterly pack is filed, retention-labelled and retrievable by quarter, entity and state.

testing.step: Pull independent extracts for the tested quarter
actions: Request the NIPR appointment listing for each writing entity directly rather than using the copy in the reconciliation pack.
Extract the producer master and the commission ledger for the same as-at date through your own query, with the field list you specify.
Compare your extract row counts to those in the pack and investigate any difference before proceeding — a filtered extract is the easiest way to make a reconciliation clean.
testing.done: independently pulled extracts exist for all three sources and their row counts are reconciled to the pack's extracts.

testing.step: Re-perform the three-way match
actions: Rebuild the join on NPN + NAIC co-code + state from your own extracts without reusing the reconciliation's workbook.
Produce the four result sets and compare each count to the reported counts.
Investigate any difference in the unappointed-production set line by line — that is the set the reconciliation is actually for.
Document the join logic used so a third party could reproduce your figures.
testing.done: the match is independently rebuilt, its four counts compared to the reported counts, and every unappointed-production difference investigated.

testing.step: Draw and document the break sample
actions: Take 100% of unappointed-production breaks and 100% of breaks carried forward from a previous quarter.
Take 25 breaks at random with a recorded seed across the remaining categories, stratified by category.
Add 15 rows from the fully matched set to test that matches are genuine and not the product of a loose join.
Record population sizes, strata, seed and draw date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample covers all severe and aged breaks, a random spread of other breaks, and a matched-set control group, reproducibly.

testing.step: Verify sampled matches against the state record
actions: For each sampled matched row, pull the producer's PDB report and confirm the appointment exists for that company and state with an effective date on or before the quarter end.
Confirm the appointment lines cover the lines the producer actually wrote in the quarter.
For each sampled break, confirm the break was real and not a join artefact from a co-code or state-code mismatch.
Screenshot the PDB appointment section into the workpaper for each sampled row.
testing.done: each sampled match and break is confirmed against PDB, with join artefacts identified and reported.

testing.step: Recompute the exposure on unappointed production
actions: For each unappointed-production break, extract every application, bind and endorsement by that producer in that state and compute the exposure window from the first transaction to the appointment effective date.
Sum written premium and commission paid inside the window from the policy and commission systems independently of the reconciliation's figures.
Compare to the impact the reconciliation recorded; understatement is itself an exception.
Check whether the state was one where appointment is required before the first application rather than after, which lengthens the exposure.
testing.done: exposure windows, premium and commission are independently recomputed per break and compared to the recorded impact.

testing.step: Test resolution quality on sampled breaks
actions: For each sampled resolved break, obtain the evidence of resolution — a NIPR appointment or termination reference, a corrected producer record, a merged duplicate — and confirm it does what the resolution note claims.
Recompute days from break identification to resolution and compare to the 5- and 30-business-day thresholds.
Confirm every carried-forward break has the Producer Compliance Manager's written approval with a stated reason and target date.
Flag any break closed on assertion without an underlying transaction reference.
testing.done: every sampled resolution is evidenced by a real transaction or record change, with days-to-resolve recomputed against threshold.

testing.step: Test the timeliness and completeness of the reconciliation itself
actions: Compare the certificate signature date to quarter end plus 20 business days for every quarter in the period.
Confirm all writing entities and all authorised states appear in the NIPR listing used — a missing state means a whole unreconciled book.
Confirm the commission extract used state of risk rather than producer home state; a home-state basis silently hides cross-border production.
Confirm the fee reconciliation was performed and signed by Finance.
testing.done: each quarter's reconciliation is confirmed complete in entity and state coverage, correctly based, signed and delivered inside 20 business days.

testing.step: Test whether root causes actually reduced
actions: List the root causes raised as process issues in prior quarters with their agreed control changes and dates.
Confirm each control change was implemented — pull the validation rule, the queue service level change or the added field and see it live.
Compare the break count for that root cause in the following quarter to the quarter it was raised in.
A control change implemented with no reduction in breaks is reported as an ineffective remediation, not a closed issue.
testing.done: each prior root-cause remediation is confirmed implemented and its effect measured in the following quarter's break counts.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, exposure and owner
actions: Raise one issue per exception with the quarter, break category, NPN, state, exposure window, premium and commission.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list: extract filtered, join artefact, break understated, resolution unevidenced, break aged past threshold, state omitted from listing, remediation ineffective.
Assign an owner and a remediation date, and refer material unappointed production to Regulatory Counsel for the state notification decision.
Carry open issues into the next semi-annual test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with quarter, category, exposure, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compare the re-performed unresolved break rate to the 1% threshold and count unappointed-production breaks against the zero threshold.
State the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper reference behind each figure.
Have the independent reviewer, who neither prepared the reconciliation nor resolved any sampled break, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Distribution Compliance forum with the recomputed exposure and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with the re-performed break rate, unappointed-production count, conclusion and reporting date is filed in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the IDD conduct procedure set — conflicts of interest, product oversight and governance, demands and needs, IPID, remuneration and complaints — and the annual review that Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/2359 Art. 4 requires

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/2359 Art. 4 (written conflicts-of-interest policy appropriate to size and organisation, identifying the circumstances and the procedures, reviewed at least annually) and Art. 5, read with IDD (EU) 2016/97 Art. 17; the product-oversight leg read against Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/2358 and the IPID leg against Implementing Regulation (EU) 2017/1469

In-scope processes.value: The written procedure estate governing IDD conduct: conflicts of interest in IBIP distribution, inducements assessment, product oversight and governance including target market and distribution strategy, demands-and-needs and suitability/appropriateness, IPID production, remuneration design, and complaints handling

In-scope systems.value: The procedure register in the GRC platform holds each procedure with owner, version, approval date and next review date, linked to the IDD obligation and to the controls that evidence it; published texts sit in the document management repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: IDD Conduct Procedure Governance Standard — the procedure inventory mapped article by article, the drafting and approval route, the mandatory annual review with the conflicts register refresh, the change-triggered review, and the communication and training cascade

Compliance procedure approved.value: Each procedure approved by its named executive owner and the conflicts-of-interest policy approved by the Board or its delegated committee; the governance standard itself approved by the Head of Compliance and reviewed annually

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual review — every IDD conduct procedure must be reviewed and re-approved within 12 months of its last approval, with the conflicts-of-interest policy review completed and minuted before the financial-year-end governance report, plus out-of-cycle review within 60 days of any relevant EIOPA guidance, national implementing measure or material business change

Deadline reminders configured.value: GRC workflow alerts to the procedure owner at 90, 60 and 30 days before the next review date, with an overdue list to the Head of Compliance monthly and an automatic out-of-cycle task raised by the regulatory-change feed

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Every approved version with its version number and approval minute, the review record showing what changed and why, the conflicts register snapshots and the training completion records retained 7 years from supersession

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any procedure past its review date, any IDD article with no owning procedure, and any conflict identified in practice but absent from the policy's circumstance list is logged with owner, cause and closure date
