Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: The full IDD conduct procedure inventory with version, approval date and review date, joined to the article-by-article obligation map and to the conflicts register entries and complaints root causes arising in the year

Pass/fail thresholds.value: 100% of IDD conduct procedures reviewed and approved within 12 months; zero IDD articles unmapped to an owning procedure; any conflict or inducement pattern evidenced in the business but absent from the policy is an individual fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is an annual review; testing runs annually after the review cycle closes, with a mid-year check that out-of-cycle triggers raised in the first half were worked

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not own or have drafted any IDD conduct procedure in the inventory

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual IDD procedure-governance workpaper (inventory extract, article coverage map, review-date recomputation, content re-performance notes, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository under Market Conduct Compliance

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Current approved texts of each conduct procedure with version history and approval minutes, the article coverage map and the conflicts register — producible for an NCA conduct-of-business review or a market conduct exam within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager fronts NCA and DOI conduct enquiries; Regulatory Counsel clears any submission of a procedure text and any statement about historical versions

checklist.step: Map every IDD conduct obligation to an owning procedure
actions: Build a coverage map with one row per obligation: IDD Arts. 17-20 (best interests, conflicts, remuneration, IPID, demands and needs), Arts. 25-30 (POG, IBIP conflicts, inducements, suitability and appropriateness), Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/2358 and 2017/2359 articles, and Implementing Regulation (EU) 2017/1469.
Against each row name the procedure that carries it, the executive owner and the control that evidences it.
List any obligation with no owning procedure as a gap and raise it as a tracker issue the day it is found.
Register the map in the GRC platform linked to the IDD regulation record so the coverage is reportable.
checklist.done: every named IDD and delegated-regulation obligation maps to an owning procedure, owner and control, with gaps raised.

checklist.step: Write the conflicts-of-interest policy to the Art. 4 structure
actions: Draft the policy so it is appropriate to the firm's size and organisation and to the complexity of the IBIPs distributed, as Art. 4(1) requires.

Identify by reference to the specific distribution activities the circumstances that give rise, or may give rise, to a conflict entailing a risk of damage to customer interests — for example the firm gaining financially at the customer's expense, having an interest in the outcome distinct from the customer's, receiving an inducement from a third party, or being incentivised to favour one product over another.

Specify the procedures to manage each circumstance and the measures to prevent it: information barriers, separate supervision, removal of direct remuneration links, declining to act, and disclosure as a last resort.
Send the draft to Regulatory Counsel and the Sustainability Risk Manager where sustainability preferences bear on the product set, and to the Chief Risk Officer for risk comment.
checklist.done: the policy names the circumstances by activity, gives a management procedure for each, and has been reviewed by counsel and risk.

checklist.step: Maintain the conflicts register from what actually happens
actions: Record every conflict identified in the year with the date, the activity, the customer impact risk, the management measure applied and whether disclosure was made.

Feed the register from the sources that see conflicts in the wild: complaints root causes, sales-quality reviews, gifts and hospitality declarations, inducement assessments and remuneration exception approvals.
At each policy review compare the register's circumstance types to the policy's circumstance list and add anything the policy does not already name.
Report register volumes and themes to the Risk & Compliance Committee at least annually.
checklist.done: the register captures dated real conflicts with their management measure, and its themes are compared to the policy's circumstance list at review.

checklist.step: Keep the product oversight and governance procedure current
actions: Ensure the POG procedure sets out, per Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/2358: target market identification at a sufficiently granular level, product testing including scenario analysis, the distribution strategy consistent with the target market, and the monitoring and review cycle for each product.
Set the trigger list for a product review — claims ratio movement, complaint volumes, lapse and surrender rates, sales outside the target market — with named thresholds rather than adjectives.
Define the information the manufacturer must give distributors and the information distributors must return, and how sales outside the target market are reported back.
Confirm the procedure names the committee that approves a product and the evidence pack it must see.
checklist.done: the POG procedure carries granular target-market rules, numeric review triggers, the manufacturer-distributor information exchange and a named approval committee.

checklist.step: Keep the demands-and-needs and suitability procedure current
actions: Ensure the procedure requires a demands-and-needs statement before conclusion of every contract, and a personalised recommendation explaining why the proposed product best meets those demands and needs where advice is given, per IDD Art. 20.

For IBIPs, set out the suitability assessment inputs — knowledge and experience, financial situation including ability to bear losses, investment objectives including risk tolerance and sustainability preferences — and the appropriateness test where no advice is given.
Specify the suitability report content and when it must be given to the customer, and the rule that no recommendation is made where the necessary information is not obtained.
Define the sales-quality sampling that tests the procedure in practice, its sample size and who reviews it.
checklist.done: the procedure mandates a demands-and-needs statement, the IBIP suitability inputs including sustainability preferences, the suitability report and a defined sales-quality sample.

checklist.step: Keep the IPID, disclosure and remuneration procedures current
actions: Ensure the IPID procedure holds the Implementing Regulation (EU) 2017/1469 format rules — the standardised layout, headings and icons, two sides of A4 as a rule, plain language, and the requirement that it is a short standalone document.

Ensure the disclosure procedure carries the Art. 18 and Art. 19 content: identity, register and verification, advice basis, holdings and links, and the nature and basis of remuneration — fee, commission, or other.

Ensure the remuneration procedure prohibits arrangements that conflict with the duty to act in the customer's best interests, including targets and incentives that could encourage a recommendation of a particular product where another would better meet the need.
Route each text to Regulatory Counsel and to the local language service for each host state where it is used.
checklist.done: IPID, pre-contract disclosure and remuneration procedures each carry their article-specific content and are counsel-cleared and translated where used.

checklist.step: Keep the complaints procedure aligned to EIOPA guidelines
actions: Ensure the procedure sets the complaints definition, the acknowledgement and final-response timescales applicable in each host state, and the escalation to the out-of-court redress body named in the Art. 18 disclosure.
Set the root-cause coding scheme so complaints feed the conflicts register, the POG review triggers and the sales-quality programme rather than dying in a service metric.
Require periodic reporting of complaints analysis and remedial actions to senior management and the relevant governance body.
Confirm the procedure covers complaints received through intermediaries and how their data is obtained.
checklist.done: the complaints procedure sets host-state timescales, a root-cause scheme feeding conflicts and POG, and governance reporting including intermediary-sourced complaints.

checklist.step: Schedule the annual review and open the review file
actions: Set each procedure's next-review date at approval date plus 12 months and configure the 90/60/30-day owner alerts.

Open the review file at 90 days containing: the current approved text, the conflicts register extract for the year, the complaints root-cause summary, the sales-quality findings, the regulatory-change log entries touching the procedure, and any internal audit findings.
Send the file to the procedure owner with the review questions they must answer in writing.
Report the overdue list to the Head of Compliance monthly.
checklist.done: each procedure has a dated review task with a populated review file issued 90 days ahead and an overdue list reported monthly.

checklist.step: Perform the review and record what changed and why
actions: Answer in writing, per procedure: has the regulation changed, has the business or product set changed, did the conflicts register or complaints reveal a circumstance the text does not cover, did testing find the control failing, and is the text still appropriate to the firm's size and organisation.
Where the answer is no change, state the evidence for that conclusion — an unchanged text with no reasoning is not a review and will not survive an NCA challenge.
Where the answer requires change, redline the text and record the source of the change against each edit.
Attach the answers and the redline to the review record.
checklist.done: each procedure has a written review record answering the standard questions with evidence, plus a redline where change was needed.

checklist.step: Take the conflicts policy and the material changes through governance
actions: Table the conflicts-of-interest policy review at the Risk & Compliance Committee or the Board as the terms of reference require, with the register themes and the change summary.
Table any material change to the POG, suitability or remuneration procedures at the committee that owns it.
Ensure the minute records the review took place, what was considered, and the approval — a version stamp with no minute cannot evidence Art. 4(1) annual review.
Load the approved version and the minute reference into the GRC platform and set the next review date.
checklist.done: the conflicts policy and every material change carry a dated approval minute, and the approved versions are stamped in the GRC platform.

checklist.step: Publish the approved texts and retire the superseded ones
actions: Publish each approved version to the single controlled location staff and distributors read, with version number and approval date on the front page.
Move the superseded version to the archive with its effective-from and effective-to dates so the text applicable at any past date is retrievable.
Remove uncontrolled copies from team sites and shared drives and replace them with links to the controlled location.
Confirm distributors with contractual obligations to follow the procedures receive the updated text through the broker portal.
checklist.done: one controlled current version is published, superseded versions are date-stamped in the archive and distributors have received the update.

checklist.step: Cascade the changes into training and into the systems that enforce them
actions: Convert each material change into an LMS module or a briefing with an assessment, targeted at the roles the change affects.
Set a completion deadline of 30 days from publication and chase non-completion through line managers.

Hand the change to the Business Systems Analyst where the procedure is enforced by a system rule — a suitability question set, an IPID template, a remuneration cap — so the configuration changes with the text.
Record the completion rate and the system change reference against the procedure's review record.
checklist.done: material changes are trained with a 30-day completion deadline and any enforcing system configuration is updated with a recorded change reference.

checklist.step: Run out-of-cycle reviews on regulatory and business triggers
actions: Subscribe to EIOPA publications, national implementing measures and host-state general-good notices and screen them weekly against the coverage map.
Raise an out-of-cycle review task within 5 business days of any change touching a mapped obligation, with a 60-day completion date.
Raise the same task on material business change: a new product line, a new distribution channel, a new host state, or a new remuneration model.
Record the trigger source and date on the procedure's review history so the reason for each off-cycle version is auditable.
checklist.done: every regulatory or business trigger raises a dated out-of-cycle review task with a 60-day completion date and a recorded source.

checklist.step: Attest annually that the procedure set is complete and current
actions: Take the coverage map, the review completion status and the overdue list and confirm every mapped obligation has a procedure reviewed inside 12 months.
List any exception with its reason and its closure date and do not attest around it.
Sign the attestation and present it to the Risk & Compliance Committee with the conflicts register themes and the complaints root-cause analysis.
File the attestation with the coverage map extract that supports it.
checklist.done: a signed annual attestation with the supporting coverage map and a named exception list is presented to the committee.

checklist.step: File the procedure governance evidence
actions: File per procedure per year: approved text with version, review record with answers and redline, approval minute reference, training completion record and any system change reference.
File the coverage map extract, the conflicts register snapshot and the signed attestation alongside them.
Store under Market Conduct Compliance / IDD Procedures / <year> and apply the 7-years-from-supersession retention label.
Confirm retrieval of the text in force at any given past date works — that is what an NCA will ask for.
checklist.done: the annual pack is filed, retention-labelled, and the text in force at any past date is retrievable.

testing.step: Build the procedure inventory population
actions: Extract every procedure in the GRC register linked to the IDD regulation record, with owner, current version, approval date, next review date and linked controls.
Add procedures published in the document management repository that reference IDD but are not in the register — an unregistered procedure is outside the review cycle by definition.
Reconcile the two lists and report any procedure present in one and not the other.
testing.done: the inventory reconciles the GRC register to published IDD-referencing documents in both directions.

testing.step: Re-perform the article coverage map
actions: Read IDD Arts. 17-20 and 25-30, Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/2358, Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/2359 and Implementing Regulation (EU) 2017/1469 and build your own obligation list.
Map each obligation to a procedure in the inventory without consulting the firm's map first.

Compare to the firm's coverage map and list obligations the firm maps to a procedure that does not actually address them — a mapped-but-not-covered row is worse than an open gap because nobody is looking for it.
Record every uncovered obligation with the article reference.
testing.done: an independent article-by-article map exists and every uncovered or falsely mapped obligation is listed with its citation.

testing.step: Recompute review timeliness across the inventory
actions: For each procedure compute days between the last two approval dates and compare to the 12-month requirement in Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/2359 Art. 4(1).
Compute the 100% on-time rate for the cycle and compare it to what the attestation asserted.
Identify version stamps changed with no corresponding review record — a re-dated document is not a review.
List every out-of-cycle trigger raised in the year and recompute whether the review closed within 60 days.
testing.done: review intervals and out-of-cycle closure times are recomputed for every procedure and compared to the asserted on-time rate.

testing.step: Sample and re-perform review quality
actions: Take 100% of procedures reviewed with 'no change' and 100% of those covering conflicts, POG and suitability.
Take 8 further procedures at random with a recorded seed from the remaining inventory.
For each, read the review record and judge whether the standard questions were answered with evidence or with assertion.
A 'no change' conclusion with no evidence cited is an exception even where the text is in fact adequate.
testing.done: every no-change and high-risk procedure review is re-performed for evidenced reasoning, with the sample method documented.

testing.step: Test the conflicts policy against conflicts that actually occurred
actions: Extract the year's conflicts register entries, gifts and hospitality declarations, inducement assessments and complaints coded to a conflict root cause.
For each distinct circumstance type, search the policy text for a circumstance that names it and a procedure that manages it.
List any circumstance evidenced in the business but absent from the policy as an individual fail against Art. 4(1)(a).
Test that the management measure the policy prescribes was the measure actually applied in 10 sampled register entries.
testing.done: every circumstance type occurring in the year is found in the policy with a prescribed measure, and sampled measures match what was applied.

testing.step: Test the procedures against front-line practice
actions: Pull 25 recent sales files across advised and non-advised journeys, including at least 10 IBIP sales.

Check what the file actually contains against what the procedure requires: demands-and-needs statement before conclusion, personalised recommendation with the reason the product best meets the needs, suitability report for advised IBIPs, IPID issued in the prescribed format, and remuneration nature disclosed.
Where practice differs from the text, determine whether the text is wrong or the practice is — both are findings, with different owners.
Record the file references and the specific missing element for each failure.
testing.done: sampled sales files are tested against the procedure text with each divergence attributed to either the text or the practice.

testing.step: Trace approvals to minutes and version control
actions: For the conflicts policy and each materially changed procedure, obtain the committee or board minute and confirm it records the review, what was considered and the approval.
Compare the minute date to the version approval date held in the GRC register.
Confirm the published text in the document repository is the approved version and that the prior version is archived with effective-from and effective-to dates.
Retrieve the text in force at a randomly chosen past date and confirm the archive supports it.
testing.done: every approval traces to a dated minute, the published text matches the approved version, and a past-dated text is retrievable from the archive.

testing.step: Test the training and system cascade
actions: For each material change in the year, confirm a training module or briefing exists and pull its completion rate against the 30-day deadline.
Identify the affected population independently from the HRIS role data and check the training was targeted at all of it, not just the obvious team.
Where the procedure is enforced by a system rule, confirm the configuration change reference exists and inspect the live rule — an updated document with an unchanged question set changes nothing.
Quantify the days between publication and system change for each.
testing.done: each material change shows targeted training with completion measured and, where applicable, an inspected live system rule change.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and due date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the procedure, the article affected, and whether the defect is coverage, timeliness, review quality, cascade or practice divergence.

Assign a root cause from a fixed list: obligation unmapped, owner not resourced, review performed as a re-date, register themes not fed back, trigger feed missed, training not targeted, system rule not changed.
Assign an owner and a remediation date, and refer any uncovered obligation with live customer impact to Regulatory Counsel.
Carry open issues into the next annual test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has an issue naming the procedure and article, with root cause, owner, remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compare the recomputed review-timeliness rate to the 100% requirement and count uncovered obligations against the zero threshold.

State the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper reference behind each figure, and state explicitly whether Art. 4(1)'s annual conflicts-policy review was evidenced.
Have the independent reviewer, who owns and drafted none of the inventory, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Risk & Compliance Committee alongside the annual attestation and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper stating the timeliness rate, coverage gaps, the Art. 4(1) conclusion and the committee reporting date is filed in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the annual MCAS submission end to end — participation determination, data build, validation, officer attestation and state-by-state filing — with Market Conduct Compliance owning the narrative interrogatories

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — the current NAIC MCAS Data Call and Definitions for each participating line, re-read on publication each year, together with each participating state's data-call bulletin; the conduct rationale sits under IDD (EU) 2016/97 Arts. 14 and 17 and the EIOPA complaints-handling guidelines requiring complaints analysis and reporting of root causes and remedial actions

In-scope processes.value: Annual market conduct data reporting: participation testing against each state's premium threshold by line, extraction of policy, claim, complaint, lawsuit and producer data for the prior calendar year, validation, interrogatory drafting, attestation and submission

In-scope systems.value: Submission through the NAIC MCAS application in iSite+/Regulatory Data Collection; source data drawn from the Policy Administration Platform, Claims Platform and the complaints system into the enterprise data warehouse where the MCAS staging build sits

Compliance procedure documented.value: MCAS Reporting Procedure — participation determination by state and line, per-element data lineage to the Data Call definitions, the validation and variance pack, interrogatory drafting and legal review, officer attestation and the post-submission state enquiry path

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Statutory Reporting Manager and the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager; re-approved each year within 30 days of the NAIC publishing the new Data Call and Definitions

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual — the MCAS submission covering the prior calendar year is due 30 April for the standard lines, with any line-specific date and the participating-state list taken from that year's NAIC Data Call and Definitions; participation is tested against the state's written-premium threshold (commonly $50,000 in the state for the line in the data year)

Deadline reminders configured.value: Milestone tasks at 15 January (participation determination), 28 February (first full data build), 31 March (validation and interrogatories complete), 15 April (attestation) and 25 April (all states submitted), with daily countdown reporting to the Regulatory Reporting Manager through April

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Participation worksheet, source extracts with run timestamps, the element-level mapping to the Data Call definitions, validation and variance packs, interrogatory responses, the signed attestation and every state submission confirmation retained 7 years from the filing date

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any state missed or filed after the deadline, any post-submission restatement, and any validation failure overridden without documented rationale is logged with the state, the element, the cause and the corrective filing

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every late or amended filing, every validation override and the root-cause remediation feeding the following year's build

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every state-line combination where the entity wrote premium in the data year, joined to the participation determination and to the submission confirmations, plus the reported element values traced back to the source policy, claim and complaint systems

Pass/fail thresholds.value: 100% of required state-line submissions filed by 30 April; element-level reconciliation to the source systems must agree within 0.5% or be explained; any missed state and any unexplained variance above 5% year on year is an individual fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual; testing runs once per year on the completed submission before the deadline where possible, with a pre-submission validation review in the first half of April and a post-submission confirmation sweep in May

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have built, validated or submitted any part of the MCAS filing

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual MCAS test workpaper (participation re-performance, element reconciliation to source, interrogatory review, submission confirmations, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository under Regulatory Reporting

Regulator-ready documentation.value: The submitted MCAS data files by state and line, the element-to-source lineage, the validation pack and the signed attestation — producible for a state MCAS follow-up enquiry or a market conduct exam data-integrity request within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Reporting Manager answers state MCAS data queries and files amendments through the NAIC MCAS application; Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager owns any resulting market conduct exam or targeted enquiry, with Regulatory Counsel clearing restatement narratives

checklist.step: Read the current-year Data Call and Definitions on publication
actions: Download the current NAIC MCAS Data Call and Definitions for every line the entity may report — private passenger auto, homeowners, life, annuity, long-term care, health, disability income, lender-placed, travel, private flood and any newly added line.
Diff this year's definitions against last year's element by element and list every added, removed or redefined element.
Read the participating-state list and each state's own data-call bulletin for state-specific deviations.
Circulate the change list to the data build owner, Claims, Complaints and Distribution within 10 business days of publication.
checklist.done: the current Data Call is downloaded, diffed element by element against last year, and the change list is circulated.

checklist.step: Determine participation state by state and line by line
actions: Extract direct written premium for the data year by state, by line and by writing company from the statutory annual statement state page.
Apply each participating state's premium threshold for the line (commonly $50,000 direct written premium in that state in the data year) and mark each state-line combination in scope or out.
Check whether the state requires a filing even below threshold, and whether it requires a zero or exemption filing rather than silence.
Record the determination per state-line with the premium figure and the threshold applied, and have the Regulatory Reporting Manager approve it by 15 January.
checklist.done: every state-line combination has a documented in-scope or out-of-scope determination with the premium figure and threshold, approved by 15 January.

checklist.step: Map every reported element back to a system field
actions: For each element in the Data Call, record the source system, table and field, the filter logic and the date basis the definition demands — written versus earned, received versus closed, calendar-year versus policy-year.

Resolve the definitional traps explicitly: what counts as a claim closed with payment, how a reopened claim is treated, whether a complaint received via a DOI counts once or twice, and how partial cancellations are counted.
Where no system field exists for an element, raise it as a data gap with the owning function rather than deriving it informally.
Have the Data Governance Lead sign the lineage document before the build runs.
checklist.done: every Data Call element has a signed lineage entry naming source, filter and date basis, with gaps raised rather than derived.

checklist.step: Build the policy and premium elements
actions: Extract for the data year by state and line: policies in force at year end, new business written, cancellations split by reason and by period since inception, non-renewals initiated by the company, and written premium.
Apply the Data Call's counting basis — policy count versus exposure count, and the treatment of multi-state policies — as recorded in the lineage.
Reconcile written premium in the extract to the statutory annual statement state page for the same state and line and explain any difference before proceeding.
Load the results into the MCAS staging tables with the extract run timestamp.
checklist.done: policy and premium elements are built, reconciled to the annual statement state page, and staged with a run timestamp.

checklist.step: Build the claims elements
actions: Extract claims opened, closed with payment, closed without payment, and open at year end by state and line, with the ageing buckets the Data Call specifies — commonly 0-30, 31-60, 61-90, 91-180, 181-365 and over 365 days.
Apply the definition's clock: days from date of report to date of final payment or date of denial, not internal handling days.
Separate suits opened, suits closed and suits open at year end, and identify claims closed without payment where coverage was denied.
Reconcile claim counts to the claims operational reporting for the year and explain differences before staging.
checklist.done: claim counts and ageing buckets are built on the Data Call's clock, reconciled to operational reporting and staged.

checklist.step: Build the complaints and lawsuit elements and their root causes
actions: Extract complaints received in the data year by state and line, splitting those received directly from consumers and those received via a Department of Insurance.
Apply the Data Call definition of a complaint precisely — an expression of dissatisfaction, whether or not it was upheld — rather than the narrower internal definition used for service metrics.
Attach the root-cause coding to each complaint so the same population supports the IDD Art. 17 and EIOPA-guideline analysis of recurring causes and systemic conduct issues.
Produce the root-cause summary with the remedial actions taken for the senior-management and governance-body report.
checklist.done: complaint counts split by source are built to the Data Call definition and the root-cause and remedial-action summary is produced.

checklist.step: Run the validation and variance pack
actions: Run the internal validation rules: no negative counts, closed claims not exceeding opened plus prior open, complaint counts not exceeding claim counts by an implausible factor, ratios inside expected bands, and totals footing across sections.
Produce a year-on-year variance report per element per state and require a written explanation for any movement above 5%.
Compare ratios — claims closed without payment, complaint rate per 1,000 policies, suit rate — to the prior year and, where available, to published MCAS ratio benchmarks for the line.
Circulate the pack to Claims, Complaints and Underwriting owners for element sign-off before submission.
checklist.done: the validation pack runs clean or with documented overrides, and every variance above 5% has a written explanation signed by the element owner.

checklist.step: Draft the interrogatory and narrative responses
actions: Draft the narrative responses the Data Call requires — for example the description of the complaint-handling process, the claim-settlement practices and any explanation of unusual ratios.
Ground each answer in the written procedure that governs it and reference the procedure version, so the narrative and the procedure estate cannot diverge.
Have Regulatory Counsel review every narrative before it is loaded — MCAS narratives are read in market conduct exams and become the standard the examiner holds the firm to.
Record the reviewed version and the counsel clearance date.
checklist.done: every narrative response is drafted against a named procedure version and carries a dated counsel clearance.

checklist.step: Load and run the NAIC application validations
actions: Log in to NAIC iSite+ and open the MCAS application under Regulatory Data Collection for the company and data year.
Upload the data file per line per state in the required format and run the application's validation.
Work every error and every warning to closure — record the rationale where a warning is legitimately accepted rather than dismissing it silently.
Save the validation output as evidence with its run date before the final submit.
checklist.done: the NAIC application validation runs with all errors cleared and every accepted warning documented, with the output saved.

checklist.step: Obtain the officer attestation
actions: Review the submission summary, the variance explanations and any validation warnings accepted before signing.
Sign the attestation the Data Call requires, confirming the data is complete and accurate to the best of the officer's knowledge and belief.
Have the Regulatory Reporting Manager confirm in writing that the element owners have each signed off their sections first.
Complete the attestation by 15 April so submission is not held hostage to a signature in the final week.
checklist.done: a dated officer attestation is on file by 15 April with element-owner sign-offs behind it.

checklist.step: Submit to every required state and capture the confirmation
actions: Submit each state-line filing through the MCAS application by 30 April, working from the approved participation determination as the checklist.
Capture the submission confirmation, its timestamp and the filing reference for each state-line, and tick it off the participation list.
File any state-specific supplementary return required outside the NAIC application through that state's own portal and record it separately.
Report the completed submission list to the Regulatory Reporting Manager the same day the last state files.
checklist.done: every in-scope state-line has a captured submission confirmation with timestamp, ticked off against the participation determination.

checklist.step: Work post-submission state enquiries and amendments
actions: Log every state query or ratio-outlier enquiry received after submission with its due date on receipt.
Investigate the element back to its lineage and source extract before answering — an answer that contradicts the filed data creates a second problem.
Where the data was wrong, file an amended MCAS submission through the NAIC application and record the amendment reference and the reason.
Notify Market Conduct Compliance of any enquiry that reads like the precursor to a targeted exam.
checklist.done: every state enquiry is logged, answered from the lineage, and any correction is filed as a recorded amendment.

checklist.step: Feed the results back into conduct governance
actions: Take the filed ratios — complaint rate, claims closed without payment, suit rate, cancellation and non-renewal patterns — to the Risk & Compliance Committee with the year-on-year movement.
Present the complaint root-cause analysis and the remedial actions taken, as IDD Art. 17 and the EIOPA complaints guidelines require, naming the systemic issues found.
Convert each systemic issue into an owned action with a date, and link it to the product oversight review triggers where the issue is product-driven.
Record the committee's decisions and track the actions to closure.
checklist.done: filed ratios and complaint root causes are reported to the governance body with named systemic issues converted into owned, dated actions.

checklist.step: Run the post-mortem into next year's build
actions: Within 30 days of the deadline, list every manual intervention, definitional judgement and late data delivery from the cycle.
Raise a tracker issue for each with an owner and a target date ahead of next year's 28 February build milestone.
Update the lineage document and the procedure with the definitional judgements made, so next year's analyst inherits the reasoning rather than re-deriving it.
Agree with the Data Governance Lead any source-system change needed to remove a manual step.
checklist.done: a post-mortem within 30 days produces owned issues dated ahead of next year's build and an updated lineage document.

checklist.step: File the MCAS evidence pack
actions: Assemble the pack: Data Call and diff, participation worksheet with premium figures, signed lineage, source extracts with timestamps, staging outputs, validation and variance packs with owner sign-offs, narratives with counsel clearance, signed attestation and every submission confirmation.
File under Regulatory Reporting / MCAS / <data year>.
Apply the 7-years-from-filing-date retention label.
Confirm retrieval by data year, state, line and element works — a state data-integrity request asks for exactly that.
checklist.done: the MCAS pack is filed, retention-labelled and retrievable by data year, state, line and element.

testing.step: Build the population of required state-line filings
actions: Extract direct written premium by state, line and writing company for the data year independently from the statutory annual statement state page.
Apply each participating state's threshold from the current NAIC Data Call and Definitions to derive your own list of required filings.
Reconcile your list to the participation determination and list every state-line the firm scoped out that your test scopes in.
testing.done: an independently derived required-filing list exists and is reconciled to the firm's participation determination in both directions.

testing.step: Reconcile every required filing to a submission confirmation
actions: Match each required state-line to a submission confirmation with its timestamp from the NAIC MCAS application.
Compute days between the submission timestamp and the 30 April deadline for each and list every late filing with its day count.
List every required filing with no confirmation at all as a missed state — the most serious finding in this control.
Check whether any state requiring a zero or exemption filing was left silent.
testing.done: every required filing is matched to a timestamped confirmation, with late day counts computed and missed or silent states listed.

testing.step: Draw and document the element sample
actions: Take 100% of elements whose year-on-year variance exceeded 5% and 100% of elements whose definition changed in the current Data Call.
Take 20 further elements at random with a recorded seed across policy, claim and complaint sections and across the five largest states by premium.
Record population size, strata, seed and draw date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample covers all high-variance and redefined elements plus a reproducible random spread across sections and states.

testing.step: Re-derive sampled elements from the source systems
actions: Read the Data Call definition for each sampled element and write your own query against the policy, claims or complaints source rather than re-running the firm's build.
Compare your value to the filed value for the state and line and compute the percentage difference against the 0.5% tolerance.
Test the definitional traps explicitly: reopened claims, DOI-sourced complaints, multi-state policy allocation, and the days-to-close clock running from date of report.
Record the query used so the recomputation is reproducible.
testing.done: each sampled element is independently re-derived from source and its difference to the filed value measured against the 0.5% tolerance.

testing.step: Reconcile filed premium to the statutory annual statement
actions: Compare written premium reported in MCAS by state and line to the statutory annual statement state page for the same data year.
Investigate every difference above the 0.5% tolerance and confirm the explanation held on file is arithmetically supported.
Confirm the same writing companies are covered in both filings — an omitted subsidiary shows up here first.
Record the reconciliation with its differences and explanations in the workpaper.
testing.done: MCAS premium ties to the annual statement state page by state and line within tolerance or with supported explanations.

testing.step: Test the complaint population against the Data Call definition
actions: Pull 30 items from the complaints system for the data year, including items the firm classified as service issues rather than complaints.
Apply the Data Call definition to each independently and determine whether it should have been counted.
Confirm DOI-sourced complaints are counted in the right split and are not double-counted when the same matter also arrived directly.
Any systematic under-counting caused by using the internal service definition is a reportable finding, not a classification difference.
testing.done: sampled complaint items are independently classified against the Data Call definition with any systematic under-count reported.

testing.step: Review the narratives and the validation overrides
actions: Read each filed narrative response against the procedure version it cites and confirm the procedure actually says what the narrative claims.
Read every accepted validation warning and its rationale and judge whether the acceptance was reasoned or convenient.
Confirm the counsel clearance date pre-dates the submission date for every narrative.
Flag any narrative that commits the firm to a practice it does not actually operate — that is an exam exposure, not a drafting issue.
testing.done: each narrative is verified against its cited procedure, every warning acceptance is judged, and pre-submission clearance is confirmed.

testing.step: Verify the attestation and the sign-off chain
actions: Obtain the signed officer attestation and confirm its date precedes the first state submission.
Confirm every element owner's section sign-off exists and pre-dates the attestation — an officer attesting over unsigned sections is a governance failure.
Confirm the attesting officer holds the title the Data Call requires.
Confirm the summary the officer reviewed matches the data actually submitted.
testing.done: the attestation is dated before submission, backed by dated element-owner sign-offs, signed by a qualifying officer over the data actually filed.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, exposure and owner
actions: Raise one issue per exception with the state, line, element, the filed value, the re-derived value and the difference.

Assign a root cause from a fixed list: participation threshold misapplied, definition change missed, lineage wrong, source extract incomplete, complaint definition too narrow, validation warning wrongly accepted, filing late.
Assign an owner and a remediation date ahead of next year's 28 February build milestone, and file an amended MCAS submission where a filed value is wrong.
Carry open issues into next year's test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with filed versus re-derived values, root cause, owner, a pre-build remediation date and any amendment filed.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Count missed and late state-line filings against the 100%-by-30-April threshold and summarise element differences against the 0.5% tolerance and the 5% variance rule.
State the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper reference behind each figure.
Have the independent reviewer, who built, validated and submitted none of the filing, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Risk & Compliance Committee alongside the MCAS ratio and complaint root-cause analysis, and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper stating filing completeness, element accuracy, the conclusion and the committee reporting date is filed in the repository.
